articleTitle: Improving Semi-Supervised Surgical Tools Segmentation with Contrastive Dual Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Accurate surgical tool segmentation is crucial for robot-assisted surgery. However, the scarcity of labelled pixel-level data hinders effective neural network training for precise instrument localization in surgical areas. This paper introduces a novel semi-supervised segmentation network with Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) and contrastive learning. By employing classifiers and projectors, positive and negative feature sets are constructed, framing the learning process as a contrastive problem. Evaluated on the Kvasir instrument dataset, our approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art semi-supervised and fully supervised segmentation models, demonstrating effective segmentation of previously unseen surgical equipment with accurate predictions.

articleTitle: Optimizing Diabetes Prediction Accuracy: A Comprehensive Approach with Advanced Preprocessing and Diverse Machine Learning Classifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Diabetes is a prevalent chronic health disease affecting millions of people over the world. Early detection and effective management contribute in preventing its complications. This study investigates the use of machine learning algorithms to predict the risk of acquiring diabetes based on multiple clinical parameters (Indian PIMA Dataset). In the study, advanced data preprocessing techniques like missing data handling, outlier rejection, robust scaling and SOMTE oversampling are consolidated with eight traditional machine learning. Effectiveness of those eight models such as Gradient Boosting (GB), XGBoost (EGB), Random Forest (RF), Light GBM (LGBM), Cat Boost (CB), Ada Boost (AB), Decision Tree (DT) and K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) are analyzed and compared. The prediction outcomes of each model are contrasted using accuracy, roc score and F1 score. After evaluating the model’s performances, GB has provided the highest accuracy of 90.25%, ROC score of 96.38% and F1 score of 86.48%.

articleTitle: IoT Based Smart Agriculture Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: In Bangladesh and the Indian subcontinent, agriculture is the backbone of any country. It is crucial for a nation’s overall economic development. Among the many social advantages of agriculture is that it meets people’s requirements for food, shelter, and employment. Most of our farmers use traditional farming practices. Agriculture-related projects on a large scale are now occurring in our country. Despite using advanced technology, they do not manage and maintain it smartly. If we handle farm management smartly, we might be able to reduce a lot of waste. Every facet of the normal person’s life has been altered by IoT technology, which imbuing everything with smart, intelligent capabilities. We demonstrated an ’IoT based smart agricultural management system’. The technology, among other things, can reduce waste of water, power, and expensive fertilizer. The device will automatically keep the soil’s fertility and moisture levels at their ideal levels. so that we can acquire the best yield feasible and exact crop growth. This technique will enable successful farming and save a lot of money and effort with manual upkeep for any project.

articleTitle: Penta-Band Near-Perfect Metamaterial Absorbers: A Butterfly-Shaped EER Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Recent statistics indicate that electromagnetic metamaterial absorbers are of great interest due to their ability to absorb nearly all incoming electromagnetic waves within a specific frequency range. The primary factor influencing absorption is the metamaterial inclusions, other than the inherent properties of the constituent material. The metamaterial absorbers (MMA) are significant because they have numerous potential applications, including manipulation of waves, terahertz imaging, harvesting of energy, operational radiatively cooling, and chemical detection. This paper presents a Penta-band near-perfect metamaterial absorber and the proposed model consists of a butterfly-shaped Elliptical Ring Resonator (EER) having four slits and which achieves a multi-band absorption from 0.1 to 3 THz range. This provides absorption of 99.44% at 1.41 THz, 99.0% at 1.92, 99.99% at 2.29 THz, 99.98% at 2.4 THz, and 92.64% at 2.64 THz. The proposed model is polarization insensitive and nearly incident angle insensitive towards 45°. This proposed model may find significant practical applications for its between the specified terahertz range.

articleTitle: A Lightweight CNN-SVM Explainable AI Approach for Classification and Visualization of Grape Leaf Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Grape is highly esteemed as a significant agricultural crop in Bangladesh. Plant diseases primarily result from the presence of pathogens and pest insects, leading to a significant decline in productivity if not properly addressed. The fundamental aim of this research is to employ a streamlined CNN-SVM architecture, utilizing deep learning techniques, to accurately categorize grape leaves into three distinct disease classes and one healthy class. The proposed model surpasses the accuracy of the previously trained transfer learning models VGG-16 and VGG-19 while having approximately $257\times$ to $267\times$ times fewer parameters (0.537 M). On average, the proposed model achieves a classification accuracy of 99.18%, which is significantly higher than the 93.42% and 91.94% achieved by the transfer learning models, respectively. With a precision, recall, and F1 score close to 99%, the suggested model provides excellent results. The model’s outstanding performance is further validated by its remarkable Area Under Curve (AUC) score of 99.98%. In addition to using less disc space (about 6 MB), the suggested model because of being lightweight shows a significant decrease in parameters. To visually display the disease identified by the proposed model, a transparent AI methodology has been utilized, specifically the Gradient Weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) technique. To better understand which area was responsible for the classification, a heatmap has been created.

articleTitle: Ensemble Learning for Improved Thyroid Disease Prediction: A Voting Classifier Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Thyroid disease represents a significant contributor to challenges in both medical diagnosis and the prediction of its onset, making it a complex area of study within medical research. This research thoroughly analyses the effective use of machine-learning approaches for thyroid identification. In our research, we use a Voting Classifier using five machine learning models: Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Decision tree, and Gradient Boosting Classifier to detect negative patients or hyperthyroid and hypothyroid patients. The combined result of multiple machine learning models refers to 99.6% accuracy which surpasses the previous results that are mostly single machine learning models. The findings indicate that when considering both accuracy and computational complexity, machine learning models emerge as a preferable option for detecting thyroid disease.

articleTitle: Advancing Water Vending Industry through RFID and IoT Empowerment
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: The provision of safe and easily available drinking water is of utmost importance for the well-being and continued existence of the human population. Nevertheless, a multitude of locations encounter difficulties in ensuring the accessibility of cost-effective and environmentally sustainable potable water. To tackle this issue, we put up a novel water vending system that incorporates RFID and IoT technologies. The focal point of the research inquiry is the provision of potable water that is both safe and affordable. This project aims to bring about a significant transformation in the water vending sector by implementing a system that improves customer satisfaction, fosters environmental sustainability, and streamlines financial operations. The approach used in this study included the utilization of RFID technology for user authentication and the customization of water distribution volumes based on individual preferences. The use of a sonar sensor facilitates a user-friendly mode of engagement, giving individuals the ability to manipulate the flow of water by manual gestures. The integration of smartphones enables the convenient process of topping up cards, hence reducing the need to use physical currency. The primary findings are improved water availability, waste reduction, and optimized financial transactions. The implementation of routine cleaning procedures and continuous monitoring of water quality guarantees the provision of clean water. This approach plays a significant role in mitigating water shortages, reducing dependence on bottled water, and promoting environmental sustainability by using biodegradable packaging. The suggested system addresses the issues associated with water vending via the use of RFID and IoT technologies. This solution provides an automated, user-friendly, and environmentally conscientious method for the provision of clean water.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of a PCF SPR biosensor for glucose concentration in urine employing external sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: This research introduces a surface plasmon sensor utilizing photonic crystal fiber (PCF) for measuring glucose concentrations in urine. The sensor employs a configuration with TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and gold as plasmonic materials, layered strategically to improve its performance. Simulation of the proposed sensor, using a finite element approach, focuses on detecting urine glucose levels. The setup involves applying a thin analyte layer onto the TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layer of the PCF to enable external sensing capabilities. Testing is conducted across four distinct glucose concentration levels: $0 \mathrm{gm} / \mathrm{dL}, 2.5 \mathrm{gm} / \mathrm{dL}, 5 \mathrm{gm} / \mathrm{dL}, 10$ $\mathrm{gm} / \mathrm{dL}$, and $20 \mathrm{gm} / \mathrm{dL}$, corresponding to refractive indices (RI) of $1.335,1.338,1.341,1.346$, and 1.358, respectively. A perfectly matched layer (PML) acts as the boundary condition for the topmost PCF layer. By adjusting geometrical parameters, an optimized structural design is achieved, resulting in a wavelength sensitivity of $3945.12 \mathrm{~nm} /$ RIU and an amplitude sensitivity of $438 \mathrm{RIU}^{-1}$ for $2.5 \mathrm{gm} / \mathrm{dL}$. Experimental validation using various urine samples demonstrates superior accuracy and sensitivity compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: Integrated Blood Donation System with Smart Vending Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: This research endeavors to address the critical challenges faced by healthcare institutions and blood centers in Southeast Asia, where an annual deficit of approximately 6 million blood units exists. The primary objective is to develop and implement an advanced blood donation management system that integrates smart technologies, communication networks, and IoT-enabled devices. The proposed system includes a user-friendly interface, a network of blood vending machines serving as smart blood banks and features such as QR code scanning, Telegram group integration, and a chatbot for efficient user engagement. By automating blood storage, retrieval, and dissemination, the research aims to enhance the overall effectiveness of the blood donation process, improve communication between hospitals and donors, and ensure the timely provision of specific blood types to patients in need. This comprehensive solution stands out as sophisticated and user-friendly outperforming existing systems in features and functionalities.

articleTitle: A Secure Vehicle Registration and Authentication System Using Distributed Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Vehicle fraud is a significant problem as the vehicle registration data can easily be fabricated and duplicated. The reason for the forgery is that in the usual registration process, car data is maintained in a centralized database, which is readily compromised. Again, the law enforcement agencies waste a large amount of time authorizing the license and registration papers. We used blockchain in our work to solve the vulnerability issues with traditional database. In this blockchain network, the data is encrypted using keccak256 hashing algorithm and the documents are secured in an IPFS network to provide topmost security. Our research also implements a secure authentication process to verify the registration and license of a vehicle owner and keep track of crime history. The use of this system will eliminate the deception of vehicle registration and traffic will be much safer with easier knowledge of vehicle fitness and crime history.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Optoelectronic Characteristics of Lead-free SrGaF3 Perovskite in the Context of Density Functional Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Investigating the characteristics and possible applications of SrGaF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> is the goal of this study. In order to perform this, the structural, optical, and electrical characteristics of the SrGaF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> perovskites were assessed using the density functional theory (DFT) approach within the CASTEP software. The computed tolerance factor and formation enthalpy verify the chemical and thermodynamic stability of SrGaF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, which was established by structural analysis. SrGaF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> has been determined to be an indirect band gap semiconductor with a band gap energy of 0.259 electron volts (eV) based on the examination of the electronic band structure. The reported band gap was validated by the density of states of the SrGaF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> perovskite structure. The structure is ductile and has good mechanical properties, according to the compound’s mechanical parameters, which include bulk modulus, Young’s modulus, and Poisson’s ratio. SrGaF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> has a greater absorption coefficient, dielectric function, and reflectivity, according to an analysis of its optical characteristics. Its suitability for use in optoelectronic devices is determined to a large extent by these features. The results of the DFT analysis indicate that SrGaF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> has a band gap that falls within the range of semiconductors. Its attractive optical properties make it an excellent choice for use in optoelectronic applications such as solar cells.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Single Layer Large Scale Microstrip Patch Array Antenna for Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: In this paper, a comprehensive study is conducted on a large-scale single layer microstrip patch array antenna with a $16 \times 16$ element configuration. The main focus is on its capability to achieve circular polarization (CP), which is crucial for long-distance wireless communication applications like Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and satellite communications. Extensive simulations are performed to evaluate the performance and effectiveness of the proposed design on Advanced Design System (ADS) software with a high-configuring computer. An initial feed circuit is designed using both-sided Microwave Integrated Circuit (MIC) technology to create a $2 \times 2$ array antenna. This design is then expanded to a $4 \times 4$ array and further implemented into an $8 \times 8$ array. By continuing this process, a $16 \times 16$ microstrip patch array antenna is constructed on a 0.8mm thick Teflon Glass Fiber substrate with a relative dielectric constant of 2.15. Having a slot in the ground plane greatly simplifies the design for feeding. The simulated results demonstrate excellent findings of the array antenna, showcasing exceptional circular polarization capabilities with an impressive impedance bandwidth of 450 MHz. Additionally, the Axial Ratio (AR) value at a frequency of 5.8 GHz stands at an impressive 0.70 dB. The proposed antenna exhibits a remarkably high gain of 47 dB in the broadside direction, having a level difference with the side-lobe gain of more than 20 dB. Additionally, it demonstrates a relative power level difference of over 20 dB in the LHCP mode indicating excellent CP performances.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Performance of Solar Photovoltaic Systems with the Capability of Sun Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Dynamic solar photovoltaic (PV) greenhouses combine the concept of agriculture with sustainable energy production. By varying sun-tracking angles, they provide greater energy production and microclimate control opportunities. Previous research on PV greenhouses rarely considered the impacts of partial shading and documented the performance over the entire range of rotation angles. This paper provides a fully documented copy of the performance of dynamic solar trackers over the day and proposes a cost-efficient model. The proposed model in this paper will reduce the generation of greenhouse gasses and eventually will participate in preventing global warming by producing clean energy, which is an eco-friendly solution to peak energy demand. Excess power can be sold to the state grid, and revenue can be generated. The model is designed using Proteus 8 professional platform and implemented practically, without using any micro-controller, to test its performance. According to the results, no-shading sun tracking produces about 22% more energy than conventional fixed PV which is highly economical. The proposed model will reduce about 50% cost than the existing models which will be highly beneficial.

articleTitle: 31-Level Asymmetric Multilevel Utility Interactive Inverter for Renewable Energy Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: In this paper, a three-phase, 31-level asymmetric, multilevel utility interactive inverter designed for renewable energy applications is presented. This inverter topology, designed with only 10 IGBT switches, features a lower number of switches compared to other 31-level inverters. A comprehensive examination of multilevel carrier sinusoidal PWM technique using phase opposition disposition (POD) is provided in this paper. A 3-phase solar powered grid connected inverter based on 31-level asymmetric Multilevel Inverter (MLI) is designed and its implementation is substantiated with PSIM<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> simulator. The control algorithm of the grid connected inverter is implemented using C language such that the control section code can be embedded directly as in the case of Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) simulation.

articleTitle: Design, Simulation, and Implementation of a Smart Net-Metering System for the Distributed PV and Grid-Connected Customers
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: The research work reports on the design, simulation, and implementation of a smart net-metering system for distributed photovoltaic (PV) and grid-connected customers. This paper presents a comprehensive study on the development and deployment of a smart net-metering system for distributed PV systems and grid-connected customers. This work aims to demonstrate the bidirectional flow of electricity for net-metered customers. Next, the paper delves into the design aspects of the proposed smart net-metering system. It discusses the architecture and components required for the seamless integration with distributed PV systems and the grid. The design incorporates advanced metering technologies, communication protocols, and intelligent algorithms to enable real-time monitoring, control, and data exchange between PV systems, customers, and the utility. The simulation and modeling of the smart net-metering system are done using MATLAB and Proteus. Various scenarios are simulated to assess the system’s performance, including energy generation, consumption, and bi-directional power flow with the grid. The results of the simulations provide valuable insights into system behavior and performance under different conditions. The implementation phase is then presented, showcasing the practical deployment of the designed smart net-metering system. The experimental hardware outlines the installation process and integration with the existing infrastructure. The experimental results show real-time outcomes of the system on the LCD screen.

articleTitle: Multiple Major Ocular Disease Classification Using Deep Learning Methods: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Ocular diseases have become an important issue worldwide. Every year, various ocular diseases affect numerous individuals, leading to blindness for many. Despite seeking treatment in hospitals or from doctors, accurately diagnosing the disease remains a challenge. In numerous cases, the correct diagnosis is elusive and time-consuming, leading to unnecessary delays. This is why computer-aided diagnosis is necessary to swiftly diagnose the disease. However, most Computer-Aided Diagnoses (CADs) are designed for single diagnoses. Therefore, there is a crucial need to develop CAD technology for detecting multiple ocular diseases. Many researchers are currently investigating this issue and developing various deep-learning models to find a solution. They have developed many techniques and models through which various types of ocular diseases can be diagnosed quickly and accurately. So far, the highest AUC score achieved is 99%. Reading all the literature on these techniques is time-consuming, so a literature review paper on this topic is necessary. In this review paper, the techniques from some important papers on this topic have been summarized. A critical analysis has been provided of all the papers, including their limitations and potential solutions.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Stimuli Response among People with Migraine Classification: A Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Recurrent, throbbing headaches are the hallmark of the neurological condition known as migraines. Other symptoms that are frequently present with migraines include nausea, vomiting, and light and sound sensitivity. This work developed a machine learning model that can almost perfectly identify migraine by analysing electroencephalography (EEG) signals. The data set used in this study consists of EEG signals recorded from 21 healthy and 18 migraine patients and obtained in three different stimuli: resting state, visual stimulus and auditory stimulus. From a total of 144 channels, 14 channels were considered as the data source. The filtered raw EEG signals were converted into raw amplitude representation within a data frame. We used a total of 3 cases for this comparative analysis by taking a single stimuli at a time, a two-stimuli hybrid approach and all three stimuli combined approach. After the basic preprocessing steps were applied, the data were fed into some Machine learning algorithms. Among the algorithms, Logistic Regression with a two-stimuli hybrid approach showed 99.74% accuracy. This approach, marked by its high accuracy, may pave the way for a reliable point-of-care solution in the diagnosis and management of migraine, offering a potential breakthrough in enhancing patient care and treatment strategies within the realm of neurological disorders. This proposed lightweight machine learning model can be effective for less calculation time and less cost.

articleTitle: Machine Learning based Identification of Cardiac Function using PCG Signal
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: The study focuses on discerning normal and abnormal cardiac function via phonocardiogram (PCG) signals, employing various machine learning models including Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Decision Tree (DT), and Random Forest (RF). Extracting features such as mean, skewness, kurtosis, and symmetry index from PCG signals, Random Forest (RF) emerged as the preferred classification model, attributed to its faster convergence time compared to SVM. Precision, recall, and F1 score were utilized to evaluate classifier performance, demonstrating high accuracy and effectiveness, particularly with Random Forest. The methodology, combining machine learning models with PCG signal feature extraction, proves effective in identifying and classifying cardiac function. Notably, the low frequency to high frequency ratio stands at 4.6329 for normal and 0.3388 for abnormal cardiac functions. This approach holds significant potential as a diagnostic tool for detecting normal and abnormal cardiac functions, crucial for effective management of cardiovascular diseases.

articleTitle: Versatile Robust DC-DC Buck-Boost Converter: Exploring Triple Configurations for Dual, Non-Inverting, and Inverting Outputs
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative design approach for a buck-boost converter circuit, utilizing a pair of inductors to enable operation within three distinct configurations. In the primary configuration, the circuit yields dual outputs, with one displaying an inverting characteristic while the other remains non-inverting. In the second configuration, the system exclusively employs an inductor to generate a non-inverting output, maintaining consistent gain like the conventional buck-boost converter. In the third configuration, an inductor is again utilized to produce an inverting output, maintaining an identical gain as the conventional buck-boost converter. Each configuration is accompanied by three distinct design conditions, ensuring stable output with exceptionally brief settling times. With various configurations and designs aimed at achieving stable output without initial oscillations, they are highly valuable in applications requiring steady voltage levels, like electric vehicle (EV) charging. The circuit’s design and analysis were conducted using Altair PSIM 2022.1 software.

articleTitle: Colon Cancer Detection Using A Lightweight-CNN With Grad-CAM++ Visualization
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Colon cancer is caused by cells that proliferate in the colon, a part of the large intestine. Early detection of cancer may make treatment easier and save many lives each year. The goal of this study is to identify improved approaches to diagnosing colon cancer rapidly and correctly. It intends to accomplish this through the use of a computer program known as a lightweight and efficient Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), which operates quickly and requires little computational power. The method may aid doctors in detecting colon cancer more successfully than earlier. The proposed model outperforms prior efforts with an amazing validation accuracy of $99.48 \%$. In our study, we employed 10,000 images from two separate classes to distinguish colon cancer cells from normal colon cells. The suggested model performs admirably, as indicated by its remarkable precision, recall, and F1-score, all of which are greater than $99 \%$, as well as its perfect Area Under Curve (AUC) score of $100 \%$. The parameters in the suggested model are lower than those in the current transfer learning models. We also compared our novel CNN model to the industry-recognized MobileNetv2 transfer learning standard to demonstrate our method’s remarkable effectiveness. To illustrate the model’s decision-making process, Gradient-weighted class activation mapping, or Grad Cam++, has been used.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Approach to Preventing Naval Accidents through Modern Signalling and Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Maritime safety remains a critical concern in the prevention of boat and naval accidents. This paper outlines a comprehensive strategy to improve marine safety by integrating contemporary tracking and signaling technology. By utilizing cutting-edge technologies, the suggested approach improves situational awareness for both boats and naval vessels by supplying real-time information. Our method builds a strong system that can recognize and reduce any threats by combining state-of-the-art tracking technology with cutting-edge signaling strategies. The system utilizes navigation patterns, vessel locations, and environmental information to prevent accidents before they happen. IoT technology is used to monitor the real-time data anywhere in the naval path and all the sensor parameters can be visualized in the web interface. Presenting a comprehensive approach that incorporates contemporary signaling and tracking technology, this study adds to the continuing conversation on maritime safety by providing a viable means of reducing the dangers connected with boat and naval mishaps in the ever-changing marine environments of today.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Five Layered Germanium-Doped Hexagonal Ring Photonic Crystal Fiber
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: This paper introduces a hexagonal five-layer photonic crystal fiber (H-PCF) design and evaluates its performance using COMSOL Multi-physics 5.5, analyzing parameters like confinement loss, birefringence, dispersion, effective mode index and effective mode area. The study examines the impact of varying contamination percentages of GeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> on SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> core and wavelengths on H-PCF characteristics. Using established formulas, calculations for dispersion, effective mode index, effective mode area, and birefringence are performed and graphically represented across different wavelengths for varying doping levels. Findings indicate consistent dispersion from $1.4 \mu \mathrm{m}$ to $1.6 \mu \mathrm{m}$, with maximal negative dispersion using 40% GeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-doped silica. GeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> enrichment substantially influences effective mode index, contributing to light confinement and total internal reflection. Increasing contamination percentage reduces effective mode area, elevating the non-linear parameter. The H-PCF design demonstrates heightened birefringence with increased doping, crucial for maintaining light polarization in communication technology. Overall, the proposed H-PCF outperforms in parameters like effective mode index, effective mode area, confinement loss, birefringence, and dispersion. Notably, at 30% GeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> doping, the H-PCF exhibits optimal characteristics for optical communication applications.

articleTitle: A Transformer-based Text-Guided Approach for Improved Colonoscopic Polyp Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Automated colonoscopic polyp segmentation, vital for early colorectal cancer detection, has notably advanced with deep learning. However, reliance on operator expertise and challenges posed by varied polyp sizes during training, along with limitations in representing long-range dependencies, warrant further refinement in the field. In this paper, we propose a novel transformer-based text guided architecture called TGA-TransNet to address these challenges. Particularly, the TGA-TransNet model incorporates size-related and polyp number-related information through text attention during training. Additionally, Transformer layers are utilized to extract global contexts. Our early experimental results on the popular Kvasir-SEG dataset indicate that the proposed integration of text embeddings and Transformer enhances the overall segmentation performance of the model, surpassing its state-of-the-art counter-part. Feature map analysis also suggests that our proposed TGA-TransNet demonstrates strong generalization capabilities across the variable-sized polyps.

articleTitle: Time Series Sales Forecasting: A Hybrid Deep Learning Regularization Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Sales forecasting is essential in diverse sectors, driving informed decision-making and efficient resource allocation. In this research, we concentrate on enhancing retail sales forecasting, specifically within the furniture industry, utilizing deep neural network models. Drawing insights from an accessible dataset containing historical sales data of a global superstore, we investigate various forecasting techniques, including classical time-series methods like SARIMA, with advanced neural network models like RNN and bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM), to capture temporal dependencies effectively. We propose a hybrid CNNBiLSTM model with regularization in BiLSTM layers to improve generalization and forecasting accuracy. Our study evaluates performance using MAE, RMSE, and $R^{2}$ score as error metrics. The results illustrate our proposed approach’s superiority with an MAE of 1.25, RMSE of 1.56, and an $R^{2}$ score of 0.53, demonstrating significant improvements in forecasting accuracy. Moreover, the introduction of regularization underscores our model’s performance, refining its predictive capabilities. This study not only unveils the potential of harnessing deep neural networks for precise retail sales prediction but also emphasizes the pivotal role of normalization techniques in nurturing robust forecasting models, holding significant implications for informed decision-making in the dynamic retail landscape and beyond.

articleTitle: Solar Panel Integration on Metro Rail Tracks for Sustainable Energy Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: The increasing worldwide need for ecologically sustainable transportation options highlights the pressing need to reduce carbon emissions in public transportation systems. This study focuses on the research issue of using solar energy for the purpose of supplying electricity to metro rail systems by the strategic placement of solar panels along the train lines. The main aim is to provide an environmentally friendly solution that effectively integrates solar energy generation and reduces the carbon emissions associated with the metro rail system. The system uses photovoltaic (PV) panels, which can directly turn sunlight into electricity. This strategy effectively harnesses the ample sunshine exposure present on metro rail lines, maximizing the natural solar capacity of these rails. The primary findings demonstrate the effective execution of this idea across many international sites through subterranean train systems driven by solar energy. These installations provide evidence to support the feasibility of using solar energy for metro rail systems, thereby enabling a sustainable and environmentally efficient form of transportation. The Internet of Things (IoT) allows real-time monitoring and optimization of systems, ensuring consistent and efficient operation. This research also highlights specific outcomes of the proposed model, revealing that solar panels installed on the Dhaka metro rail track will have the potential to generate a substantial power output of 28.7 MW. Such findings underscore the significant energy-generating capacity of solar installations on metro rail infrastructure, further enhancing the attractiveness of solar-powered transit solutions. The combination of solar energy harvesting with IoT-enabled monitoring represents a promising model for powering metro rail systems sustainably and economically.

articleTitle: Effect of Photodegrading Performance on the Structural, Optical, and Morphological properties of ZnO nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: The uniqueness of this research lies in the synthesis of ZnO NPs through a sol-gel method at 400°C, with a subsequent exploration of their photocatalytic efficiency in relation to spinning time. The investigation encompassed an in-depth analysis of the structural, morphological, and optical characteristics of ZnO NPs, employing XRD, SEM, and UV-vis spectroscopy. To assess photocatalytic performance, the degradation of methylene blue (MB) under simulated solar radiation was utilized as a benchmark. The spinning time significantly influenced the optical band gap (3.48 to 3.65 eV) and photocatalytic activity (90.4% to 96%) of ZnO NP thin films. optimized spinning time increased the surface area of ZnO nanoparticles and improved photocatalytic performance. A maximum photodegradation efficiency of 96% was achieved at 90 sec, demonstrating the potential of spin-coating with optimized spinning time for fabricating ZnO thin films with enhanced photocatalytic activity for environmental applications.

articleTitle: Modified D Shaped Dual-Band Microstrip Patch Antenna for 5G Ka Band Application
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: A dual-band microstrip patch antenna is designed and discussed in this article that operates at 28 GHz and 35 GHz frequency band which aligns with the 5G Ka band application. Two resonant cavities are formed by the antenna’s modified D-shaped design, which has a half-ring slot and a rectangular slot etched into a rectangular patch. The antenna’s return loss is computed within a range of −46.39 dB to −28.14 dB, making it suitable for 5G applications. Impedance matching is evident at 34.64 GHz and 27.68 GHz, where the antenna’s voltage standing wave ratios are 1.08 and 1.009, respectively. The suggested dual band antenna provides gains of 3.59 dBi and 6.68 dBi at 34.64 GHz and 27.68 GHz, respectively, and operates in the 5G Ka band applications, which span 26.88 GHz to 28.56 GHz and 34.10 GHz to 35.60 GHz.

articleTitle: Optimization of Different III-V Multiple Quantum Well Solar Cells with Surficial Circular Nanoholes
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Multiple quantum well solar cells (MQWSC) enhance the absorption of sunlight by allowing tunable bandgaps and improved carrier collection. This design aims to increase overall solar cell efficiency by optimizing energy conversion processes. Surficial photonic design is another approach to provide roughness which prevents reflection of sunlight from the solar cell surface and increases the optical paths of photons to reach the absorber layer. This article is focused on determining sui TableIII–V materials with structure configurations to implement in quantum wells to maximize efficiency beyond the fundamental p-n junction solar cells. Also, surficial circular nanoholes were considered to be implemented for maximizing light absorption. A total of six reported III-V semiconductor materials InP, InGaP, AlGaAs, GaSb, InGaAs, and InGaN were considered to be implemented on quantum wells. 5 layers and 25 layers of arrangements of each III-V material were investigated. Finally, the highest-performing MQWSC was incorporated with the optimized surficial nanostructure design, and the structure’s performance was compared with a fundamental single junction solar cell. GaAs solar cell is considered in this study as the host structure to implement quantum wells and surficial structure. Optical simulation was conducted to investigate light trapping enhancement using the Ansys Lumerical FDTD software. GaAs solar cells with a single junction as well as MQWSC were examined using the Ansys Lumerical CHARGE solver. It was found that the 25 layers of InP/GaAs MQWSC obtained the highest efficiency among all six III-V materials and their two physical combinations. Finally, the surficial circular nanohole design was incorporated with the highest efficient multiple-quantum well combination to obtain electrical results. The analysis shows that the 25 layers of InP/GaAs MQWSC with circular nanoholes improve the efficiency significantly from fundamental single junction GaAs solar cells. Other electrical parameters of the final design including short circuit current, open circuit voltage and fill factor hold the highest value or close to the highest value compared to the other investigated designs. The results also compared with some reported works and a notable improvement was found. This optimized design will help to construct an efficient thin-film photo voltaic device.

articleTitle: RenalNet: An End-to-End Hybrid Deep Learning and Ensemble Model for Accurate Kidney Disorder Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Kidney disorders are a major public health issue affecting millions worldwide. Renal calculi and cancer are prevalent, causing chronic kidney disease(CKD). Artificial intelligence can assist in the precise diagnosis of kidney diseases.We developed an end-to-end system using a custom CNN model to extract informative features from kidney images. Multiple ML classifiers provide complementary perspectives. A High-Performance Filter(HPF) selects the top classifiers for an ensemble model. The interactive web interface enables real-time prediction. Our approach achieves excellent performance metrics with an accuracy of 99.98%. Overall, We demonstrate an automated system combining deep learning and ensembling for the accurate characterization of diverse kidney abnormalities, which can aid in the early detection and treatment of CKD.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of T-Shaped Frequency Reconfigurable Slot Antenna for 5G Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: The emergence of fifth-generation (5G) wireless technology has attracted a lot of research interest in the development of innovative antennas to address the challenges of millimeter-wave (mm-wave) signals. To fulfill the requirements of 5G cellular communication, we propose a T-shaped frequency reconfigurable slot antenna that can easily adapt its operating frequency. Reconfigurability is accomplished through the introduction and proper biasing of a pair of PIN diodes applied across a T-shaped slot antenna element. The proposed antenna dynamically adjusts its operating frequency at 28 GHz and 38 GHz keeping both PIN diodes at OFF and ON states respectively. This reconfigurable antenna is perfect for mobile devices as it is compact with a dimension of $6 \times 3.94$ mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed antenna exhibits outstanding performance in terms of return loss, bandwidth, directivity, gain, radiation efficiency and VSWR. These attributes make it well-suited for 5G cellular communication.

articleTitle: Detecting Phishing Websites using Naive Bayes Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Phishing is one form of cyber attack used to obtain sensitive information from targeted individuals. Through this process, the attacker masquerades as a domain similar to an official legitimate website. Perpetrators can execute attacks with minimal expenses and effort, allowing them to initiate numerous assaults rapidly. The swift pace of phishing underscores the importance of automated detection processes in ensuring the protection of Internet users. Recently, many promising approaches, such as the content-based approach, heuristic-based approach, Fuzzy’s rule-based approach and machine-learning approach have been used to distinguish between phishing and legitimate ones. The existing studies do not focus on a probabilistic approach. Therefore, this study uses the Naive Bayes classification to detect phishing sites. The study compares three naive Bayes approaches: Bernoulli Naive Bayes, Multinomial Naive Bayes, and Complement Naive Bayes. The evaluation result of the Complement Naive Bayes Classifier and Multinomial Naive Bayes is superior to Bernoulli Naive Bayes. Both of the classifiers give 96 percent accuracy. As for detecting phishing websites, text classification and feature extraction are essential tasks; Naive Bayes classification provides an appropriate output.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Vanadium Dioxide-Based Terahertz Absorber
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: In this research article, we present a versatile broadband absorber employing vanadium dioxide, designed for effective absorption at terahertz frequencies. The absorber is comprised of two squares outside split rings and two elliptical resonance rings placed at a 90 -degree angle to each other at the center, utilizing vanadium dioxide $\left(\mathrm{VO}_{2}\right.$). By conducting comprehensive numerical simulations, we determine the absorption bandwidth within the specified range. Our calculations demonstrate absorption levels exceeding 90 % across frequencies ranging from 2.70 THz to 5.53 THz. Moreover, the intensity of the absorption peak can be actively adjusted, spanning from 1.8 % to 99.9 %, through continuous modulation of the conductivity of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> within the range of $2 \times 10^{2}$ $\mathrm{S} / \mathrm{m}$ to $2 \times 10^{5} \mathrm{S} / \mathrm{m}$. Notably, we observe that altering the incident angle $\theta$ leads to changes in the absorption magnitude within the asymmetric structure. The findings outlined in this research have the potential for practical applications in adjustable spectral capabilities for devices functioning within the terahertz frequency range. This includes applications in sensors, detectors, and thermophotovoltaic devices.

articleTitle: Secured Entry Control: An IoT and Deep Learning based Mask Detection System for COVID-19 Suspected Patient Screening and Access Regulation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: The new coronavirus SARS-CoV-2, which triggered the COVID-19 pandemic, has had an unparalleled effect on economies, cultures, and world health. In response to the critical need for strict COVID-19 screening systems in public areas, this study presents a creative Secured Entry Control system. Detecting and controlling possible COVID-19 carriers attempting to enter the country is made possible by this system, which makes use of deep learning algorithms and IoT technology. The mask detection algorithm, MobileNetV2 model, has an exceptional validation accuracy of $98.96 \%$. The model’s reliability is supported by performance evaluations using ROC curves, confusion matrix analysis, and an AUC value of $98.96 \%$, which is close to the optimal AUC score of $100 \%$. Because MobileNetV2 is well-suited for low-processing devices, it is easy to deploy it on Raspberry Pi, which helps to create an affordable system. Furthermore, by spotting increased body temperatures, a contactless temperature sensor improves the system’s ability to identify possible COVID-19 carriers. The functioning of the system is confirmed by the working prototype that is presented in the Experimental Results section. The main goal of this research is to create an autonomous system that is affordable and selectively allows access to people who are less likely to transmit COVID-19 in public areas. To achieve the overall objective of reducing the spread of COVID-19 in public spaces, this research highlights the successful integration of mask identification algorithms and IoT.

articleTitle: 1D Beam Switching Four Element Microstrip Patch Array Antenna with Planar 90° Hybrid Coupler
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: This paper designs and simulates a $2 \times 2$ microstrip patch array antenna for one-dimensional beam switching applications in the sub-6 GHz 5G frequency band. It incorporates a planar 90° hybrid coupler to generate a signal with phase difference between two parallel microstrip lines. A vertically flipped “T”-shaped slot line, measuring 0.1 mm in width, has been cut in the ground plane to create a “Magic-T” junction in the middle of the design. This allows the in-phase and out-of-phase signals to propagate separately along the slot line of the ground plane, while the hybrid circuit and patch are positioned on top of the Teflon Glass Fiber substrate. At the Magic-T junction, the $\Sigma$ and $\Delta$ signals from the coupled parallel microstrip lines are split apart and sent to the patches that have a phase difference. According to the simulated findings, the antenna can switch its beam up to a maximum of ±17° throughout the frequency range of 3.44 GHz to 3.60 GHz while maintaining a main lobe gain of more than 20 dB and a side lobe level differential with a main lobe gain of more than 10 dB.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Evaluation of MIMO Antenna for UWB Applications Using Four Spanner Shaped Patches
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: In this paper, a new geometry of Multiple Input and Multiple Output (MIMO) antenna for Ultra Wide Band (UWB) applications has been presented on $44 \times 44 \times 1.6$ mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> Rogers RO3003 (lossy) dielectric substrate, whose permittivity is 3. The antenna has been featured with four spanner shaped patches, arranged orthogonally. Additionally, there has been brought out a Defected Ground Structure (DGS) at the antenna’s ground, which was intended to improve isolation among the elements of the antenna to lessen interference or cross-talk problem. All the results and outcome mentioned in this paper in favour of our proposed design, were obtained from CST studio suite simulation. The operating bandwidth (BW) of the antenna was found 25 GHz, ranging from 2.69 GHz to 27.54 GHz. Additionally, the Diversity Gain (DG) was observed ≤10 dB and the Envelop Correlation Coefficient (ECC) was found 1.68e-7 for this suggested geometry. Also the average isolation performance was found −54.98 dB. Furthermore, the maximum radiation efficiency and total efficiency was recorded 80% and 85% respectively for this suggested design geometry.

articleTitle: A UWB Antenna for Wireless Body Area Network and its Characteristics Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: A newly designed small, almost square shaped Ultra Wideband antenna is presented in this paper. Free space simulations provided promising results with a wider bandwidth and high efficiency up to 97.68% within the UWB range. The antenna was intended for Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN) application. To verify its human on-body performance, a 3D human torso phantom was created and re-simulated the results by placing the antenna in its near field. To determine the effects of the presence of the human body, further distance-based studies were done by placing the antenna in five different distances from the torso phantom. The results were compared with each other and with free space simulations to determine how the distance influences its behaviors. Highest gain was recorded while the antenna was placed on 4mm and above with maximum value of 8.13dB. The results were summarized in terms of antenna parameters such as return loss, voltage standing wave ratio, farfield and 2D radiation patterns, efficiency, and gains. The antenna shows operability in wide frequency range within the UWB spectrum with optimistic gain values.

articleTitle: IoT Based Smart Headgear for Motorbike
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: A smart headgear is a type of protective helmet used by the rider which makes bike driving safer than before. In today’s world, a noticeable increase in daily road accidents is attributed to motorcyclists’ non-compliance with helmet usage. This study aims to address and prevent such accidents by emphasizing the importance of wearing helmets. The Advanced headgear design incorporates an IR sensor to detect helmet usage and an Alcohol sensor to identify whether the user is under the influence. If alcohol is detected, the bike’s ignition is automatically turned off, ensuring safe riding conditions. The ignition is activated only when the user wears a helmet and is not under the influence of alcohol. Utilizing Nodemcu and various sensors such as IR sensor, Vibration sensor, GPS module, and MQ-3 Alcohol sensor. This work utilizes the concept of the Internet of Things (IoT). This concept of advanced headgear can be implemented globally offering enhanced safety for motorcycle riders and potentially saving numerous lives.

articleTitle: Analysis of a New High-Performed Terahertz Metamaterial Absorber for Refractive Index Sensor Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: This paper reports on the design and analysis of a metamaterial perfect absorber-based terahertz refractive index sensor. The absorber material consists of a polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) substrate, with a gold resonator layer on top and a transmission-blocking ground layer deposited beneath the substrate. The primary simulation is performed using the Computer Simulation Technology (CST) software, which determines that the peak absorption occurs at a frequency of 0.74 THz and reaches a value of 99.95%. The outcome is diverse while employing the COMSOL Multiphysics software, although the outcome appears comparable. The outcomes are independent of different polarized waves such as Transverse Electric (TE), Transverse Magnetic (TM), or Transverse Electromagnetic (TEM) waves. The metamaterial absorber exhibits complete stability concerning THz waves’ polarization and incident angle. This work also examines the analysis of the material’s electric field (E), magnetic field (H), and surface current. The sensor setup of the absorber is depicted along with its performance parameters. The material possesses a quality factor (Q -factor) of 370, a sensitivity of 3.55 THz/RIU, and a figure of merit (FOM) of 1775 at a frequency of 0.74 THz. The performance is also evaluated in comparison to relevant literature. The developed metamaterial absorber has significant benefits and can be effectively utilized in refractive index sensing applications.

articleTitle: Fault Detection and Classification in the IEEE 9-Bus System Integrated with Distributed Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: The importance of integrating Distributed Generation (DG) into power system networks has increased in recent years due to rising electricity demand and limited production capacity. DG provides various solutions to various challenges, including providing alternative energy sources, reduces losses in transmission & distribution, and enhancing voltage stability etc. However, it also poses difficulties such as optimal placement, sizing, as well as fault detection in the system, etc. This paper proposes a comprehensive approach to address these difficulties through DG optimization and fault detection and classification in the IEEE 9-bus System. The suggested approach optimizes the placement and sizes of DG by minimizing active power losses and improving the voltage profile. The optimal result in the IEEE 9-bus system is achieved with a 40 MW DG unit located at bus location 5. The fault detection and classification aspect utilizes Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) techniques to identify abnormal conditions and provide accurate and quick responses to maintain the desired level of reliability in the power system. The proposed approach was tested on different case studies in the MATLAB/SIMULINK environment. The proposed method can quickly detect and respond to all types of power system faults without errors, ensuring the stability of the power system. The research findings have significant implications for the optimal integration of DG in power systems and the development of effective fault detection and classification methods.

articleTitle: Circular Split SRR Cornered by Staircase Shaped Metamaterial Absorber for 5G and X Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: A Unique circular split shape with a subwavelength-sized, high effective medium ratio (EMR=λ/L) of 14.29 metamaterial (MTM) absorber is proposed that achieves double negative MTM properties with co- and cross-polarization insensitivity up to 90°, which can be applied for 5G applications and Starlink Receiver Antenna efficiency improver. We get absorption of 99.74%, 98.26%, 91.30%, 99%, and 98.54% at 3.5 GHz, 4.88 GHz, 8.57 GHz, 10.7 GHz, and 11.88 GHz, respectively, with the refractive index being negative with permittivity and permeability showing near zero and negative properties. The dimension of the absorber is 0.07λ x 0.07λ which is compact in shape and can also be used for sensing applications. In the future, the study may be extended to explore the use of Nonlinear and Quantum Metamaterial absorbers, which will allow us to investigate how the nonlinear features of materials can be utilized to control absorption characteristics.

articleTitle: A Slotted Patch Antenna for 5G Applications Operating at 28 GHz and 37 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: In the current age of wireless communication, technology plays a pivotal role by facilitating swift and secure data exchange, our study presents a pioneering dual-band slotted patch antenna customized for 5G mobile communications. This antenna, with dimensions of 7.91×7.85×0.32 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, integrates four rectangular slots and a single circular slot, meticulously positioned on the radiating surface. The design and evaluation were carried out on a Rogers RT6002 (lossy) substrate, featuring a relative permittivity of 2.94 and a loss tangent of 0.0012, through simulations conducted in CST Microwave Studio software. The analysis yielded impressive outcomes, including return losses of -36.45 dB and -22.81 dB, gains of 5.87 dBi and 5.404 dBi, and impedance bandwidths of 686 MHz and 1.983 GHz at resonant frequencies of 28 GHz and 37 GHz, respectively. Additionally, the study elaborates on the voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) and the radiation patterns on the E-plane and H-plane of the antenna. Given its superior performance, this antenna is highlighted as a strong and viable candidate for future 5G mobile communication technologies.

articleTitle: A Comb-shaped Corrugated Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna with a Parasitic Patch for UWB Application
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: This paper presents a performance comparison of a comb-shaped Vivaldi antenna for ultrawideband (UWB) applications, which is antipodal in nature. The antenna utilizes a $50 \Omega$ microstrip feed line for energizing the antenna. To achieve ultrawide-band behavior, a parasitic elliptical-shaped patch and corrugated slots are employed. The patch controls frequency shifting along with high-gain behavior via electromagnetic coupling. To validate the proposed antenna, Rogers RT5880 substrate is used $\left(\varepsilon_{r}=2.2\right.$, tan $\left.\delta=0.0009\right)$. The proposed antenna operates in a frequency range from 5 to 28 $\mathbf{G H z}$, with the highest gain of 12.5dBi at 27.5GHz. It has a total radiation efficiency of $97 \%$ at 21.25GHz. The proposed Vivaldi antenna is a suitable candidate for high-gain wireless applications. The CST Studio Suite is employed to extract the simulation results of the antenna.

articleTitle: Design of Data – Driven Linear Quadratic Regulator Controller for DC – DC Boost Converter Optimized by Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: In this paper, a linear quadratic regulator (LQR) controller has been manifested for controlling the output voltage of a DC – DC boost converter (DDBC). Genetic algorithm (GA), a data-driven optimization technique, is used to optimize the LQR controller’s parameters. To assess how well the designed controller performs, simulation is used first. Then, based on the outcomes of the simulation, the GA optimized LQR (GA – LQR) controller provides better performance and dynamic stability under load variation, disturbed input supply voltage, and other environmental circumstances. Finally, a comparative analysis has been depicted between GA optimized LQR (GA – LQR) and conventional PID controller in terms of settling time, overshoot, and undershoot. MATLAB/ Simulink software package is used for optimization and simulation purposes.

articleTitle: Design of a Circularly Polarized 4-element MIMO Antenna for 5G Sub-6 Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: A 4-element multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna, which has circular polarization (CP), is presented in this paper for 5G sub-6 band applications. In the arrangement of MIMO antenna, a single element has a square shaped microstrip patch antenna with 2 diagonally truncated corners, a quarter-wave transformer, a microstrip line, and an inverted T-shape slot in the ground. The purpose behind the use of two truncated corners is for CP, and a quarter-wave transformer is placed for better matching of impedance. In this MIMO configuration, each antenna is set up with the next adjacent antenna orthogonally. 4 inverted T-shape slots in the ground layer and the orthogonal positions are to provide high isolation. The placement of the slots helps to expand the axial ratio’s bandwidth in single as well as MIMO antennas. The reflection coefficient and the axial ratio of the MIMO antenna are -73.34 dB and 0.97 dB, respectively. It provides an isolation value of <-35 dB along with gain values of 7.59 dBic and 7.62 dBic. The results of the diversity gain (above 9.985 dB) and envelope correlation coefficient (<0.003) are satisfactory. CST software is utilized for both design and simulation.

articleTitle: A Smart Hybrid Renewable Energy-Based Micro System for Optimal Agriculture Irrigation Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: The intricate tapestry of Bangladesh’s history comes with a myriad of challenges that have been woven into the fabric of its development. Convenient power generation is a crying need for the swift march of population growth that impedes the ongoing economic evolution. Renewable Energy is a potential panacea for the voracious appetite for energy needs, with solar and biomass appearing as suitable candidates, bearing in mind the nation’s agricultural landscape, with summer being the primary season all year. The paper embarks on a journey through the verdant expanse of 50 bighas of agricultural land, a canvas having four 2-kilowatt pumps primarily focused on developing a hybrid system utilizing biomass, solar Power, and batteries. The HOMER software used here provides the five best possible optimal system configurations. The facility discussed here can handle 11.52 kWh /day for primary consumption and a maximum energy draw of $10.29 \mathrm{~kW}$. With the exception of irrigation, the remaining Energy will be processed and supplied to the electric grid via a net metering scheme integrated with IoT and humidity sensors. A metering scheme monitors the current and voltage associated with a solar cell’s recharging from the sunlight within a battery.

articleTitle: Elderly Safety and Communication: An IoT-Based Smart Glove for Fall Detection and Hand Gesture Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Nowadays, elderly people face some physical challenges: the first is the risk of falling, and the second involves difficulties in mobility and vocalization due to advanced age. Consequently, many elderly individuals encounter obstacles in raising their voice to seek assistance with pressing needs like accessing water or attending to bathroom requirements. The objective of this work is to integrate a dual-functionality IoT-enabled smart glove, emphasizing two pivotal aspects: fall detection and hand gesture communication. Initially, the system employs an MPU6050 sensor module containing a 3-axis gyroscope and a 3-axis accelerometer, linked to an Arduino UNO microcontroller for fall and hand gesture detection. Subsequently, the microcontroller is integrated with a WiFi module (esp8266), and thirdly, the IFTTT applet is employed to showcase the messages. The glove can detect falls, and elderly individuals can call for assistance by gesturing. The microcontroller, WiFi module, and buzzer work collaboratively to promptly notify designated individuals via SMS and email, with results conveniently displayed on an LCD screen.

articleTitle: An Interpretable Machine Learning Approach for Identification of the Risk Factors of Early-Stage Overweight and Obesity
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: The increasing overweight and obesity rates pose a significant risk to public health globally, as it is closely associated with various diseases and higher rates of morbidity and mortality. Prompt and effective intervention in the early stages is therefore crucial. Furthermore, identifying obesity risk factors is essential to combat the growing rates of several secondary health problems such as cardiovascular disease, type II diabetes, and other comorbidities. This study aims to unveil the key factors playing a remarkable role in shaping this situation, utilizing the immense potential of machine learning methods. The proposed pipeline implements feature selection using Recursive Feature Elimination to effectively reduce the dimensionality of the dataset. The extracted subset of the original secondary dataset is then employed to train different state-of-the-art machine learning classifiers, including Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Decision Trees, along with the proposed novel stacking ensemble model. The proposed model outperforms other models, achieving a noteworthy accuracy of 99.58% with an AUC score of 1.0, when combined with the SMOTE-ENN balancing technique. Additionally, model explainable tool SHAP is used to rank the features according to their individual contribution, providing a more in-depth explanation of how each feature impacts the model outcome. By leveraging advanced machine learning algorithms and extensive datasets, this approach can significantly improve early-stage obesity prediction by uncovering its underlying causes.

articleTitle: Discovering the Depths of Cotton Leaf Disease Detection: Integrating Hypertuned Residual Networks with GradCAM XAI for Enhanced Understanding and Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Cotton plays a pivotal role in the textile, medical, and oil industries and is considered the world’s leading cash crop. Numerous agriculture-based countries, textile sectors, and people’s livelihoods rely heavily on cotton for their economic importance. However, the hazards posed by pests, fungi, viruses, and bacteria forming different cotton leaf diseases enormously reduce cotton production. Hence, prompt detection and identification using advanced machine learning technology has assumed enormous importance for detecting crop diseases for agricultural sustainability and the broader economic landscape. Therefore, this paper is going to present a perceptive comparative analysis of Residual Neural Networks (ResNets) with Grad-CAM XAI (Explainable AI) heatmaps to identify the most effective model used to address the pressing issue of cotton leaf disease detection. Specifically, we compare and evaluate six sophisticated ResNet transfer learning models to foster a deeper understanding of their strengths and limitations, paving the way for advancements in cost-effective, efficient, and accurate disease detection. We demonstrate a clear understanding that ResNet101V2 has the best performance (96.9%) for its model depth, skip connections, and other architectural nuances when comparing other ResNet models. Also, we integrate the Grad-CAM XAI model fostering transparency, understandability, and insights into the decision-making processes of models for facilitating collaboration with humans. By undertaking this comparative and explainable investigation, we aim to furnish a comprehensive and optimal model for the accurate identification in agricultural management practices particularly for cotton leaves disease detection to avoid the lucky choice.

articleTitle: Video Based Vehicle Detection and Tracking using Image Processing and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: With the number of vehicles on the road expanding rapidly, it is imperative to maintain sophisticated vehicle systems and traffic management. To decrease the frequency of accidents, traffic management strategies that promote highway safety and pinpoint the causes of collisions should use vehicle identification and monitoring. A new elevated highway vehicle data set containing around 8,000 images extracted from videos with proper annotation is made from the perspective of Bangladesh which provides a complete data foundation for vehicle detection and tracking based on image processing and deep learning. Classification of the vehicle is done into 10 categories. For detection purposes, the YOLO v 5 model, MASK R-CNN model, and SSD(Single Shot Detection) have been used while YOLO v 5 performs better among all. For tracking, we have used the YOLO v 5 model, DeepSORT framework, and GOTURN method where YOLO v5 is ahead among all. Following identification and tracking, the Yolo V5 model is used to estimate speed and count the number of vehicles. To verify the suggested strategy, multiple highway-monitored recordings are taken in different areas of Bangladesh.

articleTitle: Theoretical Performance Analysis of High-Efficiency Inx Ga1-xN/Si Tandem Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Owing to its intriguing optical and electrical characteristics, the $\mathrm{I}\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{x}}\mathrm{G}\mathrm{a}1-\mathrm{x}\mathrm{N}$ alloy is being widely considered as a possible silicon (Si) combo for developing low-cost, high-efficiency multi-junction solar cells. This work reports the theoretical design and performance analysis of $\mathrm{I}\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{x}}\mathrm{G}\mathrm{a}1-\mathrm{x}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{S}\mathrm{i}$ double junction tandem solar cells utilizing the wxAMPS simulator. The variation of In concentration, active layer thicknesses, and doping levels are considered to achieve optimized $\mathrm{I}\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{x}}\mathrm{G}\mathrm{a}1-\mathrm{x}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{S}\mathrm{i}$ tandem solar cells that produce superior efficiency. Our proposed solar cells have an impressive efficiency ($\eta$) of 32.92%, a fill factor (FF) of 89.49%, a short-circuit current $(\mathrm{J}_{\mathrm{s}\mathrm{c}})$ of 12.32 $\mathrm{m}\mathrm{A}/\mathrm{c}\mathrm{m}^{2}$, and an excellent open-circuit voltage $(\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{o}\mathrm{c}})$ of 2.99 V. These findings of the $\mathrm{I}\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{x}}\mathrm{G}\mathrm{a}1-\mathrm{x}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{S}\mathrm{i}$ tandem solar cells would be helpful for rethinking the design paradigm of present multi-junction solar cells and provide a path to achieving superior efficiency with a low-cost $\mathrm{I}\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{x}}\mathrm{G}\mathrm{a}1-\mathrm{x}\mathrm{N}/$Si tandem structure.

articleTitle: A Dual Band Planar Patch Antenna for WLAN and ISM Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: In this work, a dual-band planar patch (DBPP) antenna for WLAN and industrial, scientific, and medical (ISM) spectrum applications is presented. The antenna’s dimensions comprise a total volume of 28×26×1.4 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The FR4 substrate is utilized in the antenna design, leading to resonant frequencies of 2.4 GHz and 5.8 GHz. Consequently, the antenna exhibits a VSWR value of 1.0949 and 1.4802, a return loss of -27.882 dB and -15.157 dB, an efficiency of 85.14% and 64.19%, and a gain of 2.14 dBi and 2.08 dBi at these respective frequencies. The suggested antenna, with its planar geometric structure, small volume, and broad bandwidth, performs satisfactorily in the WLAN (2.4 GHz) and ISM (5.8 GHz) bands. The 5.8 GHz frequency spectrum is also used for WiMAX, RFID, and realtime audio/video signal transmission and reception applications.

articleTitle: Exploration of Structural, Electronic and Optical Properties of Be-doped BaTiO₃ Perovskite: First Principles DFT Calculations
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Perovskite materials are currently gaining a lot of attention in the field of electronics and optoelectronic device applications. This investigation explores the observation of physical properties via doping into a potential perovskite material, BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. A comparative study of structural, electrical, and optical properties of pure and doped BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> has been thoroughly examined in this work using the CASTEP code in the framework of DFT and the GGA-PBE correlation function. The findings unveil a noteworthy structural phase transition from a cubic to a tetragonal phase upon Be-doping in BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. The volume of doped BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> undergoes a reduction, shrinking from 65.40 Å<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> to 62.85 Å<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> as lattice parameters decrease. Along with a little modification of other optical properties, the band gap increased somewhat from 1.75 eV to 1.81 eV when 25% Be atoms were added to the BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. In both pure and doped BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, indirect bandgap has been observed. Notably, the dielectric function and refractive index demonstrated relatively higher values after the incorporation of Be.

articleTitle: SCCNet: An Improved Multi-Class Skin Cancer Classification Network using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Skin cancer is the most prevalent type of cancer worldwide, and detecting it early is crucial to a successful course of treatment.
