In recent years, machine learning methods have demonstrated great potential for making skin cancer detection simpler. Using a model of the fine-tuned Skin Cancer Classification Network (SCCNet) based on deep learning, we proposed a unique method for classifying skin cancer into multiple categories in this research, which is comprised of the Xception deep learning model and additional four types of fine-tuned layers. The proposed model was trained by the publicly available skin cancer dataset ISIC-2018. The dataset consists of seven classes and 21,000 images after data augmentation, with 3,000 images in each class. The proposed model achieved an accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score of 95.20%, 95.14%, 95.00%, and 95.14% respectively, for seven-class classification. The proposed SCCNet model, achieved an impressive accuracy of 95.20% in the classification of multiple skin cancer classes, outperforms several state-of-the-art approaches, demonstrating its potential to enhance dermatological diagnostics and guide effective therapeutic interventions for patients with skin cancer.

articleTitle: ANN Sensitivity Analysis Applied to Fault Classification in Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: In this paper, we apply an artificial intelligence (AI) technique to classify faults in transmission lines and analyze the sensitivity of the Artificial Neural Network (ANN). Databases were generated using Matlab<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> software for a 230 kV transmission line spanning 180 km. The ANN, implemented with the backpropagation training algorithm, was used. The results obtained from the evaluation demonstrated that the ANN exhibited satisfactory performance in fault classification, considering the sensitivity analysis of the implemented neural network.

articleTitle: Enhancing Bangla Language Next Word Prediction and Sentence Completion through Extended RNN with Bi-LSTM Model On N-gram Language
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Texting stands out as the most prominent form of communication worldwide. Individual spend significant amount of time writing whole texts to send emails or write something on social media, which is time consuming in this modern era. Word prediction and sentence completion will be suitable and appropriate in the Bangla language to make textual information easier and more convenient. This paper expands the scope of Bangla language processing by introducing a Bi-LSTM model that effectively handles Bangla next-word prediction and Bangla sentence generation, demonstrating its versatility and potential impact. We proposed a new Bi-LSTM model to predict a following word and complete a sentence. We constructed a corpus dataset from various news portals, including bdnews24, BBC News Bangla, and Prothom Alo. The proposed approach achieved superior results in word prediction, reaching 99% accuracy for both 4-gram and 5-gram word predictions. Moreover, it demonstrated significant improvement over existing methods, achieving 35%, 75%, and 95% accuracy for uni-gram, bi-gram, and tri-gram word prediction, respectively.

articleTitle: Designing a Graphics Processing Unit for 2D Rendering on FPGA for Educational Purpose
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: In this paper, design and implementation of a 2D graphics processing hardware unit using FPGA for educational purpose is presented. We propose a more simple & minimalist GPU architecture, which is flexible and easy to understand than existing industrial GPUs. We present a platform for understanding GPU architecture by implementing of graphics algorithms on FPGA for students to use this in laboratories. Students can be benefited from this work as it can be used as a base understanding tool in terms of GPU architecture. It can also be extended to be used in cross disciplinary applications like 3D rendering, computer vision and signal processing visualisation. This research includes descriptions of hardware realization of 2D rasterization rendering algorithms. Hardware Description Language (HDL) called verilog is utilized in designing the architecture. Xilinx Vivado Design Suite software is used for FPGA implementation, targeting Artix 7 FPGA board, which allows users to comprehend the fundamental ideas of hardware design and their applications in graphics rendering.

articleTitle: U-Net Deep Learning Model for the Retinal Vessel Segmentation of Latest Imaging Technology OCTA Images
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Retinal vessel segmentation in Optical Coherence Tomography Angiography (OCTA) images constitutes a crucial task in ophthalmology and medical image analysis. It involves identifying and delineating blood vessels within the retinal layers captured by OCTA imaging. This segmentation task plays a pivotal role in various clinical applications, encompassing the diagnosis and monitoring of retinal diseases like diabetic retinopathy, macular degeneration, and glaucoma. Current research on retinal vessel segmentation primarily concentrates on enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of existing methods while also exploring novel approaches. The primary objective of this research is to evaluate the outcomes resulting from the application of the U-Net model on the ROSE (Retinal OCT-Angiography Segmentation) dataset. This involves a comparative analysis of its performance against alternative segmentation models such as FCN, DeepLab, and Gated-SCNN. Experimental results demonstrate that the U-Net model surpasses FCN, Gated-SCNN, and DeepLab, achieving an accuracy of 92.73%. Furthermore, this model exhibits notably high scores in Jaccard (0.2322), Dice (0.4645), and F1-score (0.3750), indicating substantial overlap between predicted and ground truth vessel regions. Moreover, the Area Under Curve (AUC) score of the U-Net model (0.68) surpasses that of other models, signifying its exceptional performance.

articleTitle: Quantitative Analysis of Photonic Crystal Fiber Gas Sensors: Sensitivity Metrics for Benzene and Sulfur Trioxide
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: A form of optical fiber known as PCF uses the photonic crystal feature to its advantage. The quantitative effect of guiding characteristics on material properties along wavelength is examined using the finite element method (FEM). By employing the finite element method, Gas sensors made of photonic crystal fiber (PCF) can detect a variety of dangerous chemicals across a broad spectrum of wavelengths. The relative sensitivity, confinement loss, effective area and effective material loss are some of the sensing metrics obtained for two different gases by means of this gas sensor. The hazardous gases that are analyzed for the sensor investigation encompass Benzene $\left(\mathrm{C}_{6} \mathrm{H}_{6}\right)$ and Sulfur Trioxide $\left(\mathrm{SO}_{3}\right)$. The sensitivity of the proposed PCF for these two gases C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> and SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> at the frequency of 1.2THz are $94.065 \%$ and $91.433 \%$ approximately. The effective material loss is about 0.014884 and $0.026544 \mathrm{~cm}^{-1}$ and at the same frequency confinement loss are $9.95 \times 10^{-22}$ and $1.01 \times 10^{-17} \mathrm{~dB} / \mathrm{cm}$. Due to its high sensitivity and uncomplicated construction, the suggested sensor has the potential to be used in significant ways for detecting the accused object as well as biochemical and biological analytes.

articleTitle: A survey of applications of simple and multiple linear regression in solar power generation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to present the results of literature survey on the application of simple and multiple linear regression (to be called regression henceforth in this paper) technique in solar power generation. A structured literature search was conducted, and applicable papers were distinguished, checked on, and summed up. A broad publications assessment directed that the main applications of the technique could be grouped into publications on solar output power and on solar irradiance. Furthermore, the survey observed that the interest on the use of this technique has been increasing in the recent past, and this could be linked to the increased global interest in the use of solar power generation. The survey adds to literature by providing a broad overview of the papers and as a source of references on application of regression techniques in solar power generation studies.

articleTitle: Enhancing Defect Recognition: Convolutional Neural Networks for Silicon Wafer Map Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Convolution Neural Network (CNN) has been utilized to automate time-consuming and manually detecting wafer map failure root causes to improve productivity and yield enhancement in the semiconductor industry. This research provides a reliable method for detecting defects from multiclass images of wafer mapping. The overall research content can be stated as, we used random sampling to extract a total of 902 images through the combination of the original dataset for each class. Then a Deep Convolution Neural Network model was proposed to generate a multiclass classification model along with Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping(grad-cam) to highlight the region of an image that contributes to neural network prediction and f1score to evaluate its performance. Then a comparison was made between the proposed model and three other popular deep learning models-VGGNet, ResNet, and EfficientNet and showed that our proposed model outperformed those. Thus, the experimental results show a high accuracy of 91.7% and confirms CNN effectiveness in wafer map failure recognition offering a reliable efficient solution for optimizing semiconductor manufacturing.

articleTitle: Secure Wireless Multicasting with MRC Diversity in the Neyman-Pearson Receiver
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: This paper focuses on the secure wireless multicasting under the employment of Neyman-Pearson receiver with maximal ratio combining (MRC) diversity technique. MRC diversity technique mitigate the fading effect significantly. The authors set the goal for the protection of the transmitted signal from wire-trapper considering the effects of the number of multicast users, number of eavesdropper, quantity of the antenna at the receiver and quantity of the antenna at the eavesdropper end. Authors derived the closed form analytical expressions for probability of non-zero secrecy multicast capacity (PNSMC) and the secure outage probability for multicasting (SOPM) to ensure security in the presence of multiple eavesdroppers. These mathematical models are useful for the realization of the effects of aforementioned parameters. The numerical results show that, the security in multicasting employing Neyman-Pearson receiver with MRC diversity technique is significantly affected by the number of multicast users, eavesdroppers and the antennas at the multicast users and eavesdroppers specially at low noise power region of eavesdropper channel.

articleTitle: Voltage Harmonics Mitigation of Non-linear Loads using Model Predictive Control in a Three Phase System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: The escalating integration of non-linear loads, driven by the proliferation of electronic devices, has given rise to a pressing concern—harmonic distortion in three-phase power systems. This paper addresses the critical need for effective voltage harmonics mitigation strategies to alleviate adverse impacts on power quality and system reliability. Leveraging the power of model predictive control (MPC), our research aims to revolutionize the approach to harmonics suppression. By dynamically optimizing control parameters in response to evolving system conditions, the proposed MPC algorithm demonstrates a proactive and adaptive solution to reduce harmonic content. Additionally, the integration of an LC filter further enhances harmonic attenuation. Simulation results underscore the viability of this approach, showcasing its potential to enhance the performance and resilience of three-phase power systems in the presence of non-linear loads. This work contributes to the advancement of control techniques crucial for sustaining the integrity and efficiency of modern power infrastructures.

articleTitle: ElectroSortNet: A Novel CNN Approach for E-Waste Classification and IoT-Driven Separation System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Recycling e-waste is paramount important because of its environmental impact and the valuable resources that can be recovered. According to the United Nations Environment Programme, there is 100 times more gold in a tonne of e-waste than in a tonne of gold ore. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture, named ElectroSortNet, for e-waste classification. The channel-based attention mechanism is provided by squeeze and excitation networks that provide improved channel dependency and access to global contextual information. Additionally, residual shortcut connections were incorporated to address the challenge of vanishing gradients in deeper networks. The proposed ElectroSortNet achieves a 97.44 % test accuracy over a novel dataset and outperforms several previous architectures. This paper also proposed an IoT-based end-to-end e-waste separation system using ElectroSortNet as the backbone, which incorporates a conveyor belt mechanism and robotic arms that separate the e-waste and non-e-waste based on the classification result of ElectroSortNet.

articleTitle: A Relative Study on the Structural and Electric Properties of Pristine and Transition Metals (Pt, Au) Doped Boron Nitride Nanocages: A DFT Insight
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: In the last few decades, research on spherical-shaped nanostructures has brought great attention to researchers because of their unique features that make them significant potential for sustainable technologies. In this research, the structural and electric properties of spherical B$_{12}{\mathrm {N}}_{12}$ fullerene along with Pt and Au doped in two distinct sites of the B$_{12}{\mathrm {N}}_{12}$ fullerenes have been investigated using the DFT approach implying B3LYP hybrid functional with LanL2DZ basis set in Gaussian 09 program. The study confirms that doping position significantly influences the system and replacing nitrogen is more convenient than replacing boron. Also, other crucial techniques that are analyzed are IR spectroscopy, and HOMO-LUMO energies gap support the suitability of N replacing by TM dopants. Considering all factors, the suitable average bond length of 1.61 Å and preferable binding energy of -6.47 eV of B$_{12}{\mathrm {N}}_{11}$-Au reveal the feasibility of this system in implying sustainable technologies, especially in biomedical applications.

articleTitle: Efficient Hyperspectral Data Compression using 3D Convolutional Autoencoder
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Hyperspectral image has large size due to abundance of spectral bands preventing efficient storage and transmission in real-time applications. This paper introduces a 3dimensional convolutional autoencoder (CAE) for hyperspectral data compression, utilizing CAE for both compression and subsequent decompression. Our method achieves improved Compression Ratio (CR) values of 982 and 960 on the KSC and Botswana datasets, along with better Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) results of 55.29 and 52.64, surpassing existing 2D convolutional autoencoder-based HSI compression. Our approach also shows negligible differences in classification accuracy between original image and the reconstructed version of the compressed image, confirming its effectiveness in real-world applications.

articleTitle: Feature Selection-Based Machine Learning Approaches for Detecting Android Malware with Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: With the involvement of technology, its negative sides are showing out drastically. As Android is an open-source platform that has nice customization, control and accessibility features cost-effectively, it attracts middle-class device users. As of 2023, Android has a 70.29% global market share. So, its insecurity has a tremendous effect on the mobile industry. This study represents how to efficiently detect Android malware in machine learning with various feature selection techniques like Correlation, Mutual Information, Chi-Square test and Recursive Feature Elimination to serve the optimization of the huge amount of information collected from different apps. Besides, these criteria are tested with different under-sampling and oversampling techniques. This research evaluates some more widely used algorithms: Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XG Boost. Among them, Random Forest surpasses all other algorithms. The output is evaluated with another dataset. Also, Explainable AI is used for the transparency of the models. This implies that Smote NC-based Mutual Information gives the highest outcome(98.5%) with an F1 score of 98% using a 10-fold cross-validation (CV) in Android malware detection.

articleTitle: Quantum Potential Perturbed Soliton Dynamics with Self-steepening and Self-frequency Shift in Cubic-Quintic Nonlinear Media
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: A soliton is a localized and self-sustaining wave generally generated in a nonlinear medium that can propagate without considerable change in its shape. Solitons have applications in communication, medical imaging, astrophysics, and fluid dynamics. In this work, we analyze the soliton behavior in a cubic ($b_{2}$)-quintic ($b_{3}$) nonlinear medium considering perturbation terms: quantum (Bohm) potential (b), self-frequency shift (SFS) $\left(b_{5}\right)$ and self-steepening (SS) $\left(b_{4}\right)$. Using the Finite Element method, the effects of these perturbation terms on the stability of the soliton pulse have been thoroughly investigated. The parametric variation and a range of normalized values for different parameters for stable soliton propagation were determined. To find out the initial values relaxation method and curve fitting techniques along with iterative approximations are used. We found that the dispersion and cubic nonlinearity can balance the self-frequency shift. Moreover, with the increase in self-steepening, the soliton tends to become deformed and there is a small variation in the soliton shape with quantum potential if other parameters are wisely chosen. Finally, the parameters $b_{1}=0.15, b_{2}=0.6, b_{3}=$ 0.5, and $b_{4}=0.1$ were found from our investigation to observe the stable soliton. This study is important as it utilizes the finite element method of solution to demonstrate the possibility of finding solutions easily considering different physical phenomena in the same medium.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a 6G Terahertz Aeronautical Antenna Based on Graphene
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Modern technology requires high data transmission for wireless communication. 6G (sixth-generation wireless) is the next generation of wireless technology, following 5G. 6G networks will be able to operate at higher frequencies than 5G networks, resulting in dramatically improved capacity and lower latency. One of the goals of the 6G internet is to allow communications with a latency of one microsecond. A patch antenna is a good choice for its tiny size and configurable frequency. Patch antennas are now popular for use in medical devices, Wi-Fi routers, mobile phones, spacecraft, and aircraft. In this paper, a novel material, Graphene based 6G antenna is proposed for THz applications. This paper proposes a triangular patch antenna for THz applications where Copper is used as ground, Rogers is used at the substrate as an insulator, and graphene is used at the patch as a conductor. The dimension of the antenna is $(23 \times 18 \times 1.6) \mu \mathrm{m}$. The performance of the proposed antenna is analyzed using CST simulation software. Based on the simulation results, The return loss of the antenna is found -95.71 dB at the 6.82 THz resonant frequency, and the VSWR of the antenna is 1.00. The Far-Field directivity of the antenna is 5.076 dBi. Therefore, the proposed antenna is suitable for aerospace applications.

articleTitle: Bangla Sentiment Analysis On Highly Imbalanced Data Using Hybrid CNN-LSTM & Bangla BERT
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Sentiment analysis is a technique that combines machine learning and natural language processing to identify the emotional attitude of a text. This is a very active research area in recent years. Bengali is the fifth most spoken Indo-European language in the world. Many people in Bangladesh use news portals and social media to gather information on various topics. We used a publicly available dataset from Kaggle. This data set consists of more negative reviews than positive reviews. We try to experiment with this dataset with different models, such as traditional ML models and deep learning models like CNN, LSTM, and the transformer model (Bangla-BERT-base). The Bangla-BERT-base achieved a notable 96% accuracy through 10-fold cross-validation. Several other performance measures are also used to evaluate our model.

articleTitle: Breast Cancer Image Classification Using External Attention Multilayer Perceptron-Based Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: The prevalence of breast cancer has led to increased interest in its classification among healthcare scholars. Deep learning techniques and self-attention-based transformers have gained popularity in breast image analysis. However, self-attention’s quadratic complexity limits its capacity and interpretability, disregarding sample-to-sample association. To address this issue, a study introduces a novel attention mechanism called External Attention Multi-Layer Perceptron (EAMLP). EAMLP utilizes two external, tiny, learnable, shared retention units implemented with linear and normalization layers. By leveraging the linear complexity of external attention, this approach reduces operational complexity while considering all data point connections. The study evaluates the proposed model’s effectiveness using two publicly available datasets: Breast Histopathology Images and the BreakHis dataset. The model’s performance is assessed using different image sizes and numbers of dense layers. Additionally, a self-attention-based transformer is experimentally tested for comparison. The results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a maximum accuracy of 95.73%.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Cryptographic Algorithm for IoT Devices based on Hybrid Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: This paper introduces a new lightweight cryptographic algorithm with a hybrid architecture that is specifically designed for securing Internet of Things (IoT) devices. The hybrid architecture uses a unique combination of one-hot encoding (OHE) and substitution-permutation network (SPN) structures to encrypt data in a computationally and memory-efficient manner. The OHE technique is a method for representing categorical variables with a binary vector that provides confusion properties in the ciphertext. The SPN networks perform both linear and nonlinear operations to enhance the avalanche effect in generated round keys and encrypted ciphertext. The memory usage and execution cycle of the proposed cipher have been evaluated using the benchmark tool ‘Evaluation of Lightweight Cryptography Algorithms’ (FELICS). MATLAB is also utilized to test the key sensitivity of several encrypted and decrypted images using histograms and correlation graphs. The results show that the cipher provides a high level of security while being suitable for use on resource-constrained IoT devices. Hence, the proposed cipher can be a security solution for various IoT applications, such as smart homes, healthcare, and industrial automation.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of a Broadband Microstrip Patch Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: The ever-evolving cellular communication sector is constantly facing new demands. Broadband is not outside of 5G communications. In continuation of this, a compact microstrip antenna is proposed in this research. With the help of CST simulation software, a circular-shaped microstrip patch antenna has been designed with a resonant frequency of -22 dB at 28 GHz and a bandwidth of 2.4 GHz, which is suitable for broadband 5G millimeter web. FR4 lossy material is chosen as substrate, and copper-annealed material is chosen for ground and antenna patch, considering that it is helpful for 5G-related applications, and later the antenna can be practically made on a printed circuit board. VSWR is found to be 1.1, which is close to 1, and impedance matching is done at 50 ohms. At the end of the simulation, the gain is 4 dBi at the far-field directivity of 28 GHz. Overall, the compact size and performance of the proposed antenna design in terms of return loss (S11), VSWR, radiation efficiency, gain, and bandwidth are better than some published research. This design is expected to be applicable for broadband 5G applications.

articleTitle: Ziggurat Temple Shape Broadband Perfect Metamaterial Absorber for Terahertz Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: A ziggurat temple shape broadband perfect metamaterial absorber (BPMMA) has been proposed in this manuscript This absorber consists of simple five layers, made of gold at the top and bottom. Also, quartz, nickel, and alumina are in the middle layers. The BPMMA being proposed has a high absorption rate of over 90% in the frequency range of 3.322-8.209 THz On average, it absorbs 97.591% of the radiation, with a maximum absorption rate of 99.999% occurring at 6.13 THz. Additionally, this absorber is not influenced by the polarization of the incoming light and is slightly affected by the angle at which the light strikes it, also flexible up to 10°. This BPMMA has the potential for various useful applications in the terahertz range. These applications include being used as modulators, sensors, and optic-electro switches.

articleTitle: Hardware Implementations of Interleaved Modular Multiplications Over F256
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Very-large-scale integration (VLSI) of elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) is vital for efficiently securing the digital world. This research demonstrates a description of elliptic curve cryptography (ECC), with a focus on both hardware and software approaches. An effective technique is used to create a modified interleaved modular multiplication architecture that maximizes performance while minimizing hardware use. Almost 532 and 522 slice registers are available for Spartan-6 and others with 4 unique control sets each. ECC processors must carefully balance area, time, and frequency to achieve maximum efficiency, as these factors always involve limitations. In this study, a 256-bit encryption method is used with a modified algorithm for interleaved modular multiplication (IMM) in the prime field. This method requires more resources and time, but it still operates at a satisfactory speed. In addition, a new hardware circuit methodology is introduced and implemented utilizing the Xilinx ISE software on various FPGA platforms, such as Kintex-7, Virtex-5, Virtex-6, and Spartan-6. The proposed 256-bit modular multiplication design occupies only 1478, 1497, 1478 and 1483 look-up tables (LUTs) and attains noteworthy completion with 1.9 $\mu$s, 2.09 $\mu$s, 3.83 $\mu$s, and 2.11 $\mu$s on Kintex-7, Virtex-5, Spartan-6, and Virtex-6, respectively, at maximum frequencies of 134.7 MHz, 77.9 MHz, 67.097 MHz, and 121.527 MHz individually. Taking the National Institute of Standards suggested prime fields into consideration. Rigorous simulation and verification procedures are conducted employing Modelsim and Maple’s software to ensure the accuracy and reliability of the obtained results.

Author Keywords: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)

articleTitle: Highly Sensitive Dual-Core PCF SPR Biosensor for the Detection of Cancer Cells based on Fuzzy logic
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-core photonic crystal fiber (PCF) biosensor is proposed that is capable of effectively identifying cancer cells based on fuzzy logic. The suggested biosensor is investigated numerically with the Finite Element Method (FEM), and fuzzy logic is applied for the classification of cancerous cells. In the range of values for refractive index, the recommended sensor performs between 1.35 and 1.41. The range of RI values for normal cells is 1.35 to 1.37, while the range for cancerous cells is 1.39 to 1.41. The sensor exhibits high selectivity when it comes into contact with live cells by combining fuzzy rules. The suggested photonic crystal fiber sensor operates well since fuzzy rules are adjusted for it. Additionally, a cancer detection probability of 0.832 is introduced to the fuzzy logic system. The proposed biosensor displayed the highest wavelength sensitivity (WS) of 18000 nm/RIU and Amplitude sensitivity (AS) of 843.87 ${\mathrm {RIU}}^{-1}$ at y polarization mode. The proposed sensor covers the gap with high sensitivity, better detection, easy fabrication, and superior selectivity, reducing ambiguity by applying fuzzy logic. A development in technology that raises the standard.

articleTitle: Emotion Recognition from Speech Audio Signals using CNN-BiLSTM Hybrid Model
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) has recently grabbed huge attention due to its application in Human-Computer Interface, human-robot interaction, assessment of human behavior, virtual reality, and mostly noteworthy high AI-driven environments. It’s not that easy to extract emotion from human physiological information. Previously, several attempts have been made by researchers to study SER for different purposes with various audio feature variations in several approaches such as SVM, MLP, CNN, LSTM, and many other approaches. Most of the approaches use audio databases RAVDESS, IMOCAP, EMO-DB, etc. In this paper, we have focused on improving the accuracy of emotion detection from speech most precisely. For this purpose, we’ve used three datasets RAVDESS, TESS, and CREMA-D, and merged these to form a large dataset. A hybrid model using CNN and BiLSTM deep learning network is proposed to recognize eight emotions happy, calm, sad, surprised, neutral, angry, disgust, and fear. The model is trained, validated, and tested using three features: Zero Crossing Rate (ZCR), Root Mean Square Energy (RMSE), and Mel Frequency Cepstral coefficient (MFCC) extracted from raw datasets. After extensive experiments, the proposed CNN-BiLSTM model achieved the highest accuracy of 97.8% using three merged datasets.

articleTitle: Crescent-cut and Extended Circular Patch Circularly Polarized Microstrip Antenna for ISM Band Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Four circularly polarized single feed microstrip patch antennas are introduced in this paper. Circular polarization is achieved by a single crescent-cut, a single crescent extension, a double crescent-cut and a double crescent extension on a circular patch antenna. All four antennas are designed to operate in the Industrial, Scientific and Medical (ISM) band. The antennas are designed and simulated to obtain parameters by an electromagnetic simulation tool named ADS (Advanced Design System). The return loss of the single crescent-cut antenna is -20.58 dB, the single crescent extension is 16.95 dB, the double crescent-cut is -34.98 dB and the double crescent extension is -31.47 dB between 2.35 GHz to 2.45 GHz that show good input impedance matching. The axial ratios are found less than 3 dB in their resonance frequencies. Smith charts of these antennas have a dip at 2.4, 2.38, 2.42 and 2.42 GHz respectively demonstrating the ability to achieve circular polarization within the frequency range of the ISM band signifies the capability of this system. Performance analyses based on different parameters of the four antennas have been done at the end.

articleTitle: Multi-Class Skin Cancer Classification Using Modified MobileNet Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: One of the top three dangerous forms of cancer is skin cancer that can be fatal and is brought on by broken DNA. Cells develop uncontrolled way as a result of this damaged DNA, and they are growing faster. Skin lesion classification is a crucial task in dermatology as it helps in the early diagnosis and treatment of various skin diseases. To save time, effort, and human lives, early detection of skin lesions requires an automated system that can be relied upon for classification. Lower death and morbidity rates from skin cancer may result from early identification. The purpose of this work is to use deep learning with modified MobileNet architecture to classify skin lesions. The 10,015 unique images in the HAM10000 dataset, along with the associated files, were used. The well-known quantitative measurements (such as validation accuracy, sensitivity, precision, F1-score, specificity, loss, and confusion matrix) are used to test the efficiency of the proposed method. The proposed method resulted in 93.2%, 93%, 93%, 94%, 93%, 99%, and 23% respectively for validation accuracy, sensitivity, precision, F1-score, specificity, and loss. The suggested model resulted better in comparison to other transfer learning models. This proposed method can be effectively applied for robust and dependable classification of skin cancer.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Secured and Decentralized Database for Valid Students Using Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Database security is one of the most critical and major concerns facing the information and communication technology industry. It encompasses data/information availability, integrity, and confidentiality. Most of the institutions use centralized databases for their students. Centralized databases become vulnerable and inaccessible when the central server gets down. If any hacker gets access to that database, he/she can perform any fraudulent activities to the database. In this paper, we proposed a decentralized database for valid students using blockchain technology which is almost impossible to alter or modify the information for its chained cryptographic encryption feature. We used Hyperledger Fabric platform which is an opensource blockchain framework along with CouchDB database to store student’s information which will be distributed among the permissioned nodes. At last, we analyzed our model’s performance using Hyperledger Caliper tool.

articleTitle: Design of a wide-angle stable bendable dual-band metamaterial absorber in the GHz spectrum
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: A metamaterial-based ultra-thin dual-band absorber is designed in this work using three layers of materials (Copper - FR-4 - Copper) for microwave absorption in which the resonance band lies on 5.3GHz (C-band) and $13.4 \mathrm{GHz}(\mathrm{Ku}-$ band), with a bandwidth of 0.09GHz and 0.223GHz, respectively. The absorption levels are found to be $99.94 \%$ and $\mathbf{9 8. 4 \%}$, respectively. The design is numerically analyzed using the Finite Integration Technique. The structure is tested with different oblique incident angles and it provides reliable performance up to 60°. Mechanical bending analysis on the absorber performance is also done to check the reliability of the structure in harsh environments. The design is capable of showing good absorbance performance under different convex and concave mechanical bending. The field distribution of the structure is also investigated. The design can be used in $\mathbf{G H z}$ applications such as detecting the salinity of the soil, distinguishing vegetable oils from animal fat, detecting the saturation level of edible oils, and WLAN applications at the C band.

articleTitle: Intrapartum fever prediction for pregnant woman from microbial data
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: The usage of deep learning in microbial data has come a long way since its early days. For fever detection during pregnancy, this paper collects microorganism data from vaginal microbes and trains machine-learning models to classify their class, taxa, phylum, and distribution. This paper presents a novel approach to predicting the etiology of intrapartum fever in pregnant women using machine learning classifiers on vaginal microbial data. High-throughput sequencing was used to analyze a diverse dataset of microbiome abundance profiles. Various classification algorithms were employed to develop predictive models, including logistic regression, support vector machines, and random forests. The study also aimed to identify key microbial taxa or functional profiles associated with each etiology. The XGBoost algorithm emerged as the most accurate, with an accuracy rate of 86%. The study underscores the significance of features such as chills and delivery mode in predicting intrapartum fever. The findings suggest that machine learning can enhance diagnostic accuracy and guide interventions, with potential implications for improving clinical decision-making and care for pregnant women and neonates. Further research is needed to validate these findings and explore broader machine learning applications in reproductive health.

articleTitle: Real-Time Health Insights: A Smart IoT-Based Approach for Monitoring Paralysis Patients
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Paralysis, which is defined as the loss of muscle function in certain body parts, presents unique issues in healthcare, necessitating technological and medicinal advances to improve patients’ quality of life. This research proposes a novel solution a low-cost, user-friendly gadget that includes basic nursing care and a health monitoring system to alleviate the communication difficulties that paralysis patients encounter. The objective of our method is to enable patients to effectively communicate messages or requirements despite their physical constraints. Our device enables paralysis sufferers to express messages using basic motion, resulting in increased communication and interaction with caretakers. This unique device can be effortlessly integrated into their clothing or worn on their finger, providing a delicate but effective communication aid. Moreover, our smart IoT-based technology extends beyond communication to include real-time health monitoring capabilities. The system continuously collects health data by integrating multiple sensors and gadgets, providing real-time insights into vital signs and movement patterns. This real-time health information enables healthcare providers to provide prompt treatments and individualized care, hence improving the overall well-being of paralyzed patients. The proposed strategy represents a big step forward in the comprehensive treatment of paralysis patients, promoting improved communication and proactive healthcare management.

articleTitle: Novel Approaches to Achieving band Absorption in Metamaterial Absorbers for Thermophotovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: The study provides a comprehensive numerical analysis of the absorber and emitter components used in solar thermal photovoltaic (STPV) systems to convert electromagnetic energy into photons. The present analysis incorporates both theoretical dimensions and practical considerations. The absorber was made to give near-unity absorptivity over all solar wavelengths for a large angular range. This allowed it to absorb light from solar sources efficiently, regardless of concentration. It is made up of an array of nickel resonator layers, or pyramids. A sharp emissivity peak is produced at the solar cell bandgap by the emitter, a nickel slab with a Si/SiO2 multilayer stack, which simultaneously suppresses emission at lower frequencies. Our findings indicate that a STPV system utilizing an absorber-emitter pair and a single-junction solar cell can achieve an efficiency higher than the Shockley-Queisser limit when the light concentration is appropriate and the emitter-to-area ratio is fair.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual-Band Microstrip Patch Antenna for 5.9 GHz and 7.25 GHz with Enhanced Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Due to the growing need for fast transmission and large channel capacity in 5G applications, dual band patch antennas are becoming more and more common. Additionally, it can offer a reliable and robust wireless connection in hard-to-reach places. This study explores the design of a dual-band microstrip patch antenna operating at 5.9 GHz and 7.25 GHz. The proposed antenna exhibits bandwidth enhancement, addressing the growing demand for efficient 5G communication system. The use of FR-4 as material for the substrate and copper for the patch and ground contribute to the antenna’s cost-effectiveness and ease of integration. Introduction of slot in patch and ground improves antenna’s performance which also allows bandwidth enhancement by adjusting the dimensions. In this paper the enhancement of bandwidth from 31 MHz to 44 MHz gives the scope for enhancing 5G communication applications such as V2X communication, satellite and radar application.

articleTitle: A numerical analysis of a high-efficiency solar cell using a DFT explored nontoxic perovskite material
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: In recent years, Perovskites have been a very interesting breakthrough in the field of photovoltaics because of their excellent performance with easy and less complex synthesizability, and cost-effectiveness. This instance suggests a uniquely designed solar cell with a novel perovskite, Rb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> NaGaBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>. The perovskite, used as the active layer, is analyzed through the First Principle Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculation, where the cell is simulated by the SCAPS-1D simulation tool showing a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.86% for this single-junction solar cell. In order to achieve optimum efficiency, the effects of defect concentration and the thickness of the absorber layer are examined and adjusted. Here, the influence of the absorber thickness and defect concentration on fill factor, short-circuit current ($\mathrm{J}_{\mathrm{sc}}$), and open-circuit voltage ($\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{oc}}$) were also examined in addition to their impact on PCE. Based on the insights gathered from the simulation of the designed cell, $\mathrm{FTO} / \mathrm{SnO}_{2} / \mathrm{Rb}_{2} \mathrm{NaGaBr}_{6} / \mathrm{CuI} / \mathrm{W}$, the best results were obtained at a thickness of 0.8μm. The simulation indicated that $\mathrm{J}_{\mathrm{sc}}=25.02 \mathrm{~mA} / \mathrm{cm}^{2}$, a fill factor (FF) of 84.01%, and $\mathrm{V}_{\text {oc }}=1.2777 \mathrm{~V}$, that leads to a PCE of 26.86%.

articleTitle: Effect of Nb doping on structural, morphological and optical properties of solid-state sintered Na0.5 Y0.5 Cu3 Ti4 O12 ceramics
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: The numerous characteristics of sodium yttrium copper titanate (NYCTO) ceramics are strongly connected to its structure, surface morphology, and synthesis technique. This work presents the successful fabrication of Na<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf> Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf> Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> Ti<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> and Na<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf> Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf> Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> Ti<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3.99</inf> Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.01</inf> O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12.005</inf> ceramics using solid-state sintering route and provides the effect of Nb doping on microstructure, surface morphology, and optical properties. The X-ray diffraction analysis reveals that both samples exhibit a high degree of crystallinity and consist of a body-centered cubic perovskite crystal structure. There were impurity phases of CuO identified in undoped NYCTO sample. The lattice parameter was determined using the Rietveld method. The addition of Nb results in a rise in the lattice parameter from 7.381 to 7.384. The size of crystallites has been found to decrease as a consequence of Nb doping. Positive slope value of the W-H plot indicated the presence of tensile strain in the samples. Relative density has decreased from $96.42 \%$ to $93.94 \%$ with Nb doping. The Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope FESEM images shows clearly defined grains in the material, exhibiting a random range of grain sizes. The smaller grains are positioned among the larger grains. These images demonstrate how Nb doping substantially influences the surface morphology of NYCTO. The incorporation of Nb facilitated a decrease in the average grain size. The UV-visible investigation revealed that doping with Nb resulted in an increased optical absorption and a reduced band gap.

articleTitle: Performance Investigation of A Sewage Sludge-Based Terrestrial Microbial Fuel Cell (TMFC)
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Microbial fuel cells (MFC) as a substitute for generating electricity and managing waste has gained popularity. MFCs are viewed as a potential alternative for conventional power sources because they harness the power of microbes to convert the chemical energy in organic matter into electricity. This study focused on performance of a terrestrial microbial fuel cell (TMFC) that utilized easily obtainable ingredients from local markets and sewage sludge. The designed system has an anode, cathode, cathodic chamber, proton exchange system, and electrode catalyst. The process starts with assembling the unit and collecting wastes for preparing the substrate. After that, the respective solution is prepared for the anode and cathode chambers. Finally, electrodes are connected, and the voltage is measured after a specific time. Modifying the catalyst recorded the maximum voltage as 1168 mV, and the highest power generation amount was calculated as 143.1 mW/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Microbial electricity generation using MFCs could emerge as an effective form of bioenergy in the coming years, during which abundant organic waste can be reduced and valorized.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Differential Relay for Power Transformer Protection
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: This paper illustrates the design and implementation of a differential protection relay for protecting transformers in power distribution systems. Transformers are a key component of the electric power system, and protecting them is essential. Faster and more specific protection is needed since the transformer itself may sustain damage during an electrical failure. Overcurrent relays cannot provide accurate and quick operation for transformers because they use time grading and directional detection. Differential protection mechanisms are used for the above reasons. The core concept of the differential protection system is Kirchhoff’s first law, which states that the sum of the currents going to a node is equal to the sum of the currents flowing away from it. The differential protection scheme detects the difference between the current entering a segment and that leaving it. When there is a difference between entering current and leaving current, the protection is active only. The problem is that an inrush current, also known as a magnetizing inrush current, is only transitory and lasts for a few milliseconds. It is worth mentioning that the inrush current is substantially larger, ranging from two to ten times that of the transformer’s ordinary rated current. In this paper, Kirchhoff’s voltage law (KVL) is also applied with a special programming algorithm to design differential relays to overcome the inrush effect. CT and PT are used as current and voltage sensors, and the Arduino Mega 2560 R3 is programmed to perform the IEC 60255-187-1:2021 standard differential protection relay (using minimum pickup of 87T = P.U. at 0.3, slope-1 = 30%, slope-2 = 60%, and break point between slope-1 and slope-2 = 2.0, delay time: 01 cycle). The differential relay provides voltage and current protection as well as inrush current protection of the power transformer. There is a provision for storing voltage and current data for future analysis.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Formalin Detection in Fish Using Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: For the people of Bangladesh, fish is a non-vegetarian and staple food. As Bangladesh is a riverine country, fish is available everywhere in our country. Fish rots easily. For this reason, the fish has to be preserved to fulfill people’s nutritional needs. To meet the needs of the people of Bangladesh, fish is collected from the rivers and sometimes imported for this vast population. While importing fish or taking it from one place of the country to another, unscrupulous traders mixed formalin to prevent the fish from rotting. Formalin is very harmful to the human body. It creates so many health problems like cancer, miscarriage, tumors, etc. So, it is essential to detect formalin fish and non-formalin fish. There is a need for a more dependable and automated method of formalin detection because current approaches rely on human senses and are prone to inaccuracy. Digital image processing has become a promising technology for fish formalin detection in recent years. In this paper, an intelligent application is proposed. This model can identify formalin and fresh fish based on the images of fish eyes. The capability of digital image processing to offer a quick and non-intrusive examination technique is one of the main advantages of formalin detection. Without damaging sample preparation, it can swiftly and accurately identify the presence of formalin by examining photographs of the fish. This is especially helpful in large-scale operations when it is impractical to inspect each fish manually. Digital image processing algorithms are more accurate and consistent because they are not influenced by human biases or subjective judgments like human senses are. The architecture we proposed is VGG-16, and we compare it with EfficientNet-B3. VGG-16, renowned for its simplicity and effectiveness in various computer vision tasks, achieved a notable accuracy of 94.44%.

articleTitle: An Eight-Term Karatsuba Multiplier for Cryptographic Hardware Primitives on FPGAs
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: It is essential to have efficient large integer multiplications for current cryptosystems. Karatsuba-like multiplication is one of the most efficient multiplication algorithms, but is mostly avoided due to complex sub-multiplications. Thus, efforts has been made to implement eight-term Karatsuba Multiplication (Method-II), i.e., ETKM-II in terms of speed and hardware utilization. The overall performance of the proposed design methods are noted by calculating Area-Time-Product (ATP) and compared with conventional eight-term Karatsuba multiplication (CETKM) and existing state-of-the-art. Hardware implementations of the proposed ETKM multiplication architectures are done using Virtex-7 FPGA device in Xilinx ISE platform. Compared with other state-of-the-art designs the performance of the proposed eight-term Karatsuba multiplication (MethodII) based on $\Delta {ATP}_{2}$ is 13.396%, 78.206% and 38.740% better than Direct Multiplication (DM), Traditional Schoolbook Multiplication (Traditional SBM) and CETKM respectively for 1024bit inputs. However comparing the proposed ETKM-II, it can be inferred that ETKM-II is 38.740% better than CETKM thus proving its area-time-product efficiency.

articleTitle: Dosimetric Comparison of Three-Dimensional Conformal Radiotherapy and Intensity Modulated Radiotherapy in Carcinoma of Lung
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Lung cancer has prominence globally, and claims over two million lives yearly. Radiotherapy uses medical imaging to detect disease severity and spatial relationships to treat malignancies while protecting healthy tissue. Computed Tomography (CT) was employed to examine the conformity of target coverage and normal tissue sparing in the context of Intensity Modulated Radiotherapy (IMRT) and Three-Dimensional Conformal Radiotherapy (3DCRT). For each patient, objectives and organs at risk (OARs) were determined slice by slice. The Planning Target Volume (PTV) was affixed to the Multi-Leaf Collimator (MLC), and the 3DCRT treatment plan was developed utilizing the 7 fields box approach. Preparations were initiated for IMRT utilizing five gantry angles that were uniformly spaced and 6 MV beams. Our intention is to administer 50 Gy in 25 segments to each patient. Utilizing the Dose Volume Histogram (DVH), doses of the critical structures and targets for analysis were recorded. The target homogeneity of the 3DCRT and IMRT plans was comparable. Although IMRT utilized slightly more dosage volumes ($V_{5}, V_{10}$, and $V_{15}$) than 3DCRT, dose areas were larger. The IMRT plan resulted in 3.29 percent lower mean doses to the heart than the 3DCRT plan, which may indicate less cardiac damage. The average dosage administered to the spinal cord in the IMRT plan was 5.74 percent less than in the 3DCRT plan. The OAR conservation of IMRT is preferable to that of the 3DCRT plan. In the absence of IMRT or Volumetric Arc Therapy (VMAT) capabilities, centers may employ the 4 -field box approach with 15 MV beams and PTV-fitted MLC to decrease the volume of high-dose irradiation. This modification has the potential to yield a diminished toxicity profile.

articleTitle: A Custom CNN Approach for Detection and Classification of Image artefacts in Silicon Hyperbolic Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Hyperbolic metamaterials (HMMs) possess a hyperbolic dispersion profile in Fourier space (k-space), enabling deep sub-wavelength imaging over much of the electromagnetic spectrum. However, existing theoretical analysis and experimental demonstrations have shown that imaging with HMMs suffers from unwanted imaging artefacts that restrict their operation for broad-band imaging. In this paper, we study the image transmission properties of silicon-based HMMs at THz frequencies. From our numerical simulation, we show that the proposed metamaterial can resolve feature sizes below the diffraction limit but suffers from severe image artefacts. Using a convolutional neural network (CNN) we classify between good and bad images and also use a custom SqueezeNet model architecture to detect the good images. The proposed techniques can classify the good images with an accuracy of about 98%.

articleTitle: Judicial System in Bangladesh Using Distributed Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: The current judicial system process, which is conducted manually in Bangladesh, is characterized by a high degree of uncertainty and risk, as well as a wide range of possibilities for fraudulent documents and the preservation of the ownership details of cases. Therefore, the current system does not appear to be feasible, effective. We have created our proposed blockchain-based judicial management system with the SHA-256 data encryption technique. This system will ensure the safety of the case transactions and will be able to store, authenticate, and maintain entire pertinent information of the case document. The mentioned architecture will be able to revoke and to detect attempts to change the case by using a variety of technologies, including IPFS, Proof of Stack (PoS), and public-key cryptography. These techniques will lead to subsequent more efficient solutions than the existing systems and improve how the general public views Bangladesh’s judicial system.

articleTitle: Design and Linearity Analysis of a Dual Control 5-Stage CSR-VCO for RF Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: This paper presents dual control voltage in the conventional 5 -stage current-starved ring voltage-controlled oscillator (CSR-VCO) to provide a wider tuning range and fine-tuning possibilities for radio frequency (RF) applications. The circuit is implemented in $45 \mathrm{~nm}$ CMOS $1 \mathrm{~V}$ process technology. The proposed circuit is found to have an oscillation frequency range from 6.51GHz to 13.66GHz for the first control voltage $(0.8 \mathrm{~V}-1.8 \mathrm{~V})$. On the other hand, the second control voltage $(1 \mathrm{~V}-1.8 \mathrm{~V}$) demonstrates a better linear frequency range, spanning from 5.65GHz to 13.66GHz when the first control voltage is fixed at $1.8 \mathrm{~V}$. Modifying the first control voltage, in conjunction with the second, results in precise changes in the frequency level, providing the potential for fine-tuning in radio frequency applications. The 1MHz offset phase noise of the VCO at the maximum output frequency of 13.66GHz is found to be $-75.96 \mathrm{dBc} / \mathrm{Hz}$ and the corresponding power consumption is found to be $2.68 \mathrm{~mW}$.

articleTitle: Study of the application of MCSA at Induction Motors of a Roller Table
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Electric motor fault mapping techniques have been widely used to increase the performance of industrial assets. A major challenge in this scenario is the conflict between equipment that monitors assets and other electrical and electronic equipment installed in the industry, such as capacitors, inductors, among others that influence the harmonics present in the network. One of the most used techniques when we talk about electric motor diagnostics is Current Signature Analysis (ESA). ESA is a set of techniques capable of detecting faults in any electromechanical assembly by reading electrical signals. According to BONALDI et al [1], among the techniques that make up ESA, MCSA (Motor Current Signature Analysis) is the most used technique in the industrial sector and stands out for its scope and simplicity, as it only requires analyzing the harmonic spectrum signal. current of the machine, thus detecting abnormal conditions in the equipment. This article aims to demonstrate the application of MCSA and study the possible applicability of using these techniques to improve the reliability of a roller table where 268 electric motors are installed in series and which use a frequency inverter to power the motors. This starting system can make the MCSA technique difficult and this problem will also be discussed.

articleTitle: An Ensemble Based Approach for Green Area Segmentation from Satellite Images
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Recent statistics show an alarming depreciation in green space in all kinds of regions. Image segmentation using deep learning models is a promising and quick method to determine the green space of an area and aid environment specialists in taking necessary actions. Hence, the objective of this research is to compare state-of-the-art deep learning models and then propose the best approach for segmenting green space from aerial images. Traditional Deep learning and Ensemble Learning techniques were implemented with a publicly available and a self-made data set containing 5108 and 1737 images respectively. All the models were evaluated using suitable performance metrics and the Ensemble Learning approach was found to perform better. The best-performed segmentation model is obtained by incorporating Segnet, UNet and DeepLabV3+ with accuracy, precision, and dice-coefficient of 0.94, 0.96 and 0.91.

articleTitle: Incident angle insensitive dual-band epsilon-shaped metamaterial absorber for K-band and Ka-band applications
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: This paper presents an epsilon-shaped metamaterial absorber for K-band and Ka-band applications. The operating frequency range is 20.193 GHz and 30.087 GHz, with excellent absorbance of 99.5% and 99.9% for both frequencies. Also, the quality factor is high for both frequencies, 155.33 and 527.84, respectively. The structure size is minimal, 10×10 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and the design is constructed on an FR4 substrate using the simulation software CST Microwave Studio. Furthermore, this proposed absorber is compared with other existing work and this absorber is quite impressive for its good absorption characteristics. Its unique features, such as small size, excellent absorption, and high-quality factor, make it appropriate for using K-band and Ka-band applications, such as radar, satellite and mobile communication systems.

articleTitle: Optimal Equalizer Selection for umMIMO Hybrid Beamformation at 6G THz Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Recently, the use of lab testbed sampling in the real-world for the upcoming 6G era has started. In order to enhance the Bit Error Rate determination, a system that utilizes ultra-massive multiple input multiple output (umMIMO; $1024 \times 1024$) will utilize an assortment of multiplexing strategies. The data rate and system performance are increased by the umMIMO [1] system for 6G. In this study, we have concentrated on finding the optimal BER in a range of multiple access strategies to meet the requirements of equalization selection and spatial multiplexing. The equalizer should be able to handle large bandwidths and lessen the effects of frequency-selective fading because of high frequency THz transmission. For ease of use and efficiency in managing spatial interference, linear equalizers are taken into consideration, such as minimal mean square error (MMSE) equalizers or zero-forcing (ZF) equalizers. In this work, we pick the equalizer and determine spatial multiplexing using the 8PSK modulated Rayleigh, Ricean, and Nakagami fading channels. We have assessed this issue using MATLAB simulation.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of RF Absorption Perspectives in Liver and Lung Tissue Using SAR Quantification
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: RF devices are becoming essential in modern life. This type of RF absorption is becoming crucial for human health. All living things’ most vital organs are the liver and lungs. We compare how the liver and lungs absorb radiofrequency radiation to better classify organs by radiation sensitivity and enhance patient and public awareness. The experiment was controlled via simulation software. The transmitter and receiver were one metre apart, and a non-metallic stand held the goat liver and lung samples in the centre. The main data was recorded with a 10°-step size from 0° to 360°. After adding a goat liver and lung sample to the stand, the data was captured using the previous configuration. Data was recorded without samples in this arrangement. RF radiation is absorbed more by the lung sample than by the liver sample. Lung tissue’s specific properties cause this. Following this, we used MATLAB to examine the Specific Absorption Rate (SAR), and we discovered a higher graph for lung tissues. We also plotted this graph for 3D SAR visualization. A better understanding of RF absorption in the liver and lungs was achieved by comparing free space data obtained from two different organ samples. Free space data with lung sample tissues had a cross-correlation of 233.496 when analyzed for 0 degrees; however, free space data with liver sample data had a higher value of 497.019. Lung tissue samples do, in fact, absorb more radiofrequency radiation. Despite being conducted in a facility with low external $R F$ radiation, this experiment will be more effective in a completely insulated chamber.

articleTitle: Design and Numerical Analysis of a Multiband Antenna for 5G Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: A sophisticated rectangular patch antenna has been conscientiously designed for a variety of wireless applications. This proposed antenna achieves a multi-band resonant frequency response, seamlessly covering 6.97 GHz, 9.58 GHz, 14.31 GHz, 16.29 GHz, 17.57 GHz, 19.86 GHz, and 21.6 GHz. The simulation design is crafted using CST software and a high-frequency Rogers RO 4350B substrate with a slender thickness is utilized to construct a compact patch volume of $0.604 \lambda_{0} \times 0.256 \lambda_{0} \times 0.035 \lambda_{0} \mathrm{~mm}^{3}$, where $\lambda_{0}$ is a free space wavelength at 6.97 GHz. This patch employed two slotted insets along with L shape slot in the ground to provide better return loss < −10 dB for all the resonant frequencies. It also provides nearly a perfect VSWR of less than 2 to the respective bands. The resonant frequencies nestle comfortably within the C, X, Ku, and K bands, opening doors to a wide array of 5G wireless applications, particularly in WiMAX, radar and satellite communications, scientific endeavors, and industrial communication networks.

articleTitle: Drivers Real time Drowsiness, Attention Detection and Alarm System using Eye Aspect Ratio(EAR) Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: There is an immediate threat to the highway transportation system from road accidents, which can cause death, serious injury, and property damage. Accidents involving motor vehicles cause significant injury or death to a large number of individuals annually. Fatigue, lack of focus, and lethargy are key contributors to vehicle collisions. In order to identify driver inattention or exhaustion in real-time, this research lays forth a system that combines an emergency alarm system with Eye Aspect Ratio (EAR), which is based on facial landmarks. The method's strength is that it can accurately differentiate between closed eyes and inattention, even in low-light conditions. The experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method in resolving these critical issues, offering a practical means to enhance road safety.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of a High Performance Surface Plasmon Resonance Biosensor for Biosensing Application
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: This study develops a simple hybrid structure of surface plasmon biosensor and employs a suitable numerical simulation approach to assess performance. Beginning from the fundamental structure, ZnO and WSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layered-based structure is developed to get optimum performance. The optimum thickness of WSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is determined to show the minimum reflection of the structure. Sensitivity, detection accuracy, and quality factor are theoretically and numerically evaluated for the proposed SPR biosensor. The numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed optimum structure enhanced sensitivity of $\mathbf{1.1}$ times higher compared to the basic Kretschmann configuration. The highest sensitivity of 99 deg/RIU is obtained with a moderate value of detection accuracy and quality factor. Since the $\mathbf{Z n O}$-Au-based proposed sensor architecture offers a significantly improved performance, it can be effectively used in various practical applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Low-Voltage-Ride-Through in Grid-Connected DFIG-based WECSs Using an Adaptive Backstepping Control Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: To accommodate the widespread use of grid-connected wind energy systems (GCWES), grid operators frequently update grid codes to ensure improved grid stability. Wind energy conversion systems (WECS) employ low-voltage-ride-through (LVRT) as a crucial feature for sustained grid connection during transient voltage disruptions. Despite control mechanisms in place, challenges such as imbalanced phase voltage, parameter uncertainty, and insufficient reactive power assistance have been observed. Hence, this paper proposes an adaptive backstepping controller (ABC) for doubly fed induction generators (DFIGs)-based GCWES to enhance the LVRT. The controller aims to provide adequate active and reactive power to the grid for enhancing LVRT capacity, specifically addressing issues related to rotor-side converters and DC-link voltage dynamics. The proposed controller utilizes adaptation principles and it is developed iteratively through the Lyapunov control theory. Control Lyapunov Functions (CLFs) are employed to ensure convergence of physical features of DFIGs-based GCWES. Finally, MATLAB/Simulink validates the proposed approach, simulating severe faults at the wind farm’s point of common coupling and comparing results with existing controllers.

articleTitle: Cost Analysis of Virtualized BBU Pool for 5G C-RAN
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: The Cloud Radio Access Network (C-RAN) design is a viable way to resolving the encounters that upcoming 5G will face. By integrating the Radio Access Network (RAN) with cloud networking, C-RAN offers the potential to optimize resource utilization and reduce energy consumption. In this study, we create a C-RAN system that uses flexible Base Band Unit (BBU) allocation, and a power model is provided to decrease the overall power consumption of the network. A cost model is also provided in order to reduce the C-RAN’s overall cost. The research also creates analytical models for comparing the T-RAN (Traditional RAN) model with developing cloud RAN architecture. The proposed network presents improved performance compared to the conventional network, according to the numerical findings derived under simulation circumstances.

articleTitle: Four Element Wi-Fi Shaped Slot Circular Patch MIMO Antenna Design for UWB Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: This work includes the design and analysis of a four-element $\mathrm{Wi}-\mathrm{Fi}$ shaped slot circular patch multiple input multiple output (MIMO) antenna optimized for ultra-wideband (UWB) applications. Partial ground and slots in the patch offered large bandwidth along with high gain. The antenna is constructed on a FR4 lossy substrate of relative dielectric constant of 4.3. Measuring approximately $60 \times 68 \times 0.87 \mathrm{~mm}^{3}$, the MIMO antenna provides efficient integration into various wireless networks. The design’s performance features, including impedance matching, scattering patterns, gain, and surface current are thoroughly examined. The simulation findings indicates that the antenna has a large bandwidth of 9GHz covering 8GHz to 17GHz frequency range. $-51 \mathrm{~dB}$ return loss at the center frequency indicates proper impedance matching as well as high isolation from one antenna element to another element is achieved with a return loss less than $\mathbf{- 2 0} \mathrm{dB}$ over the frequency range. The MIMO antenna also offers a gain of $4.7 \mathrm{~dB}$.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface in Enhancing Security of Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: This paper delves into the security analysis of wireless communication networks incorporating reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) in the context of mathematical model of ergodic secrecy capacity. The investigation specifically focuses on scenarios with a single receiver and a single eavesdropper, operating over a Rayleigh fading channel. This study delves into the impact of parameters, including the average signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of channels and the number of reflecting elements within the RIS. Analytical expressions for the ergodic secrecy capacity (ESC) are derived, providing insights into the system’s security performance. The analysis is further extended to include a comparative study between scenarios with and without the integration of RIS. In addition to the analytical framework, the paper conducts Monte-Carlo simulations to validate the accuracy of the derived results. The obtained outcomes affirm the positive effect of employing RIS enhancing the ergodic secrecy capacity in wireless systems, particularly offering a foundation for further exploration and practical implementation in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Digitization of an Analog Kymograph
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Advancement in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (ICAEEE)
abstract: Biomedical research has been altered by the digitization of experimental setups, such as the organ bath and kymograph, by overcoming the drawbacks of conventional approaches. Potential inaccuracies and limitations in data collecting and analysis have been caused by manual measurements and subjective interpretations. The goal of this experiment is to create a dependable, user-friendly digital system that combines an accelerometer, an organ bath, and a kymograph. Real-time data capture, automatic recording, and enhanced visualization capabilities can all be accomplished by observing and analyzing mechanical movements. Accelerometer integration automates data collection, improving accuracy and productivity. Digitization has made it possible to use sophisticated visualization techniques that provide accurate and thorough depictions of physiological changes. Algorithms and software technologies allow for deeper insights into underlying processes. The precision, effectiveness, and dependability of physiological research have all significantly improved with the integration of accelerometers into experimental setups. For continued development and use of digitized systems, however, issues with accelerometer measurements, setup integration, and protocol standardization must be resolved.

articleTitle: Development of an IoT-Based Pipe Water Quality Monitoring and Control System for Smart City
